source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: All selected public labels match original source records. Complete verse records, including annotations, are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps royal ancestry, office, ten men, and the shared meal before the attack.
verses.before: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, from the royal offspring and one of the chief officers of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. They ate bread together there at Mizpah.
verses.after: In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, a man of royal descent and one of the king's officers, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah with ten men. They shared a meal there at Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, from the royal offspring and one of the chief officers of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. They ate bread together there at Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the group's attack followed by Ishmael's singular killing of the appointed governor.
verses.before: Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him arose and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword and killed the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.after: Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him rose up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword. Ishmael killed the man the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him arose and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword and killed the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the Judeans from the occupying soldiers without supplying numbers.
verses.before: Ishmael also struck all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah and the Chaldean men of war who were found there.
verses.after: Ishmael also killed all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, along with the Chaldean soldiers found there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ishmael also struck all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah and the Chaldean men of war who were found there.

verses.rationale: Lets the temporal introduction continue into the arriving pilgrims.
verses.before: On the second day after Gedaliah had been killed, before anyone knew it,
verses.after: The day after Gedaliah was killed, before anyone knew about it,
verses.tsw_comparator: On the second day after Gedaliah had been killed, before anyone knew it,

verses.rationale: Preserves all places, eighty men, mourning injuries, and offerings without explaining away the ruined sanctuary.
verses.before: eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, with their beards shaved, clothes torn, and bodies cut, carrying grain offerings and incense in their hands to bring to the house of the LORD.
verses.after: eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. Their beards were shaved, their clothes torn, and their bodies cut. They carried a grain offering and frankincense to bring to the house of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, with their beards shaved, clothes torn, and bodies cut, carrying grain offerings and incense in their hands to bring to the house of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps Ishmael's tears as narrated without labeling his motive.
verses.before: Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, walking and weeping as he went. When he met them, he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”
verses.after: Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he walked. When he reached them, he said, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, walking and weeping as he went. When he met them, he said to them, “Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.”

verses.rationale: Makes the compressed slaughter-into-cistern construction intelligible without softening it.
verses.before: When they came into the midst of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them and cast them into the cistern, he and the men who were with him.
verses.after: Once they were inside the town, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men with him slaughtered them and threw them into the cistern.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came into the midst of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah slaughtered them and cast them into the cistern, he and the men who were with him.

verses.rationale: Retains all stored commodities and the ten men's escape from the massacre.
verses.before: But ten men among them said to Ishmael, “Do not put us to death, for we have hidden stores in the field—wheat, barley, oil, and honey.” So he refrained and did not put them to death with their brothers.
verses.after: But ten of them said to Ishmael, “Don't kill us! We have stores hidden in the fields: wheat, barley, oil, and honey.” So he held back and did not kill them with the others.
verses.tsw_comparator: But ten men among them said to Ishmael, “Do not put us to death, for we have hidden stores in the field—wheat, barley, oil, and honey.” So he refrained and did not put them to death with their brothers.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult association with Gedaliah and the cistern's history; note explains the uncertain phrase.
verses.before: Now the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the dead bodies of the men whom he had struck because of Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.
verses.after: The cistern where Ishmael threw the bodies of the men he had killed alongside Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the dead bodies of the men whom he had struck because of Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

verses.rationale: Retains royal daughters and the repeated captivity verb as the situation worsens.
verses.before: Then Ishmael took captive all the remnant of the people who were at Mizpah, the king’s daughters and all the people who remained at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and departed to cross over to the children of Ammon.
verses.after: Ishmael took captive all the people left in Mizpah: the king's daughters and everyone else whom Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Ishmael took captive all the remnant of the people who were at Mizpah, the king’s daughters and all the people who remained at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and departed to cross over to the children of Ammon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator's judgment and the commanders' response to news.
verses.before: When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him heard all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
verses.after: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him heard about all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him heard all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,

verses.rationale: Reads the many waters as a large pool, identifying the location without modern reconstruction.
verses.before: they took all the men and went to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great waters that are at Gibeon.
verses.after: They gathered all their men and set out to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great pool at Gibeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: they took all the men and went to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great waters that are at Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the captives' emotional response before their movement.
verses.before: When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him, they rejoiced.
verses.after: When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders with him, they were glad.
verses.tsw_comparator: When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him, they rejoiced.

verses.rationale: Makes the change of allegiance and direction readable without adding combat.
verses.before: All the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and came back and went to Johanan son of Kareah.
verses.after: All those Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and went back to Johanan son of Kareah.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and came back and went to Johanan son of Kareah.

verses.rationale: Retains eight survivors without inventing the fate of the other two.
verses.before: Yet Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the children of Ammon.
verses.after: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the children of Ammon.

verses.rationale: Unpacks the long recovery clause while preserving all groups and both places.
verses.before: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him took all the remnant of the people whom they had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after he had struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam: men of war, women, little children, and court officials, whom he brought back from Gibeon.
verses.after: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders with him gathered the people he had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after the murder of Gedaliah son of Ahikam: the men of war, women, children, and eunuchs taken from Mizpah and brought back from Gibeon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies who were with him took all the remnant of the people whom they had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after he had struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam: men of war, women, little children, and court officials, whom he brought back from Gibeon.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form Chimham and retains the stopping place as a name.
verses.before: They went and stayed at Geruth-Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, intending to go and enter Egypt
verses.after: They went and stayed at Geruth-chimham near Bethlehem, intending to go on into Egypt,
verses.tsw_comparator: They went and stayed at Geruth-Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, intending to go and enter Egypt

verses.rationale: Keeps the reason for fear as the group's expectation, not a reported reprisal.
verses.before: because of the Chaldeans, for they were afraid of them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.after: away from the Chaldeans. They were afraid of them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of the Chaldeans, for they were afraid of them because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jezaniah here rather than harmonizing the name with 43:2.
verses.before: Then all the commanders of the armies, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest approached
verses.after: Then all the army commanders, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, came forward.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the commanders of the armies, Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest approached

verses.rationale: Preserves your God and the contrast between former numbers and the remnant.
verses.before: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, “Please let our plea fall before you, and pray to the LORD your God for us, for all this remnant. For we are left only a few from many, as your eyes see us.
verses.after: They said to Jeremiah the prophet, “Please hear our plea. Pray to the **LORD** your God for us, for all this remnant. Once we were many; now only a few of us are left, as you can see.
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to Jeremiah the prophet, “Please let our plea fall before you, and pray to the LORD your God for us, for all this remnant. For we are left only a few from many, as your eyes see us.

verses.rationale: Keeps the twofold request for direction and action.
verses.before: May the LORD your God tell us the way in which we should walk and the thing that we should do.”
verses.after: May the **LORD** your God show us the way to go and what we should do.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May the LORD your God tell us the way in which we should walk and the thing that we should do.”

verses.rationale: Retains both divine names and Jeremiah's promise of a complete answer.
verses.before: Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard. Look, I will pray to the LORD your God according to your words, and whatever word the LORD answers you, I will tell you. I will not hold back a word from you.”
verses.after: Jeremiah the prophet answered, “I hear you. I will pray to the **LORD** your God as you ask. Everything the **LORD** tells me in answer to you, I will tell you. I will hold nothing back.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah the prophet said to them, “I have heard. Look, I will pray to the LORD your God according to your words, and whatever word the LORD answers you, I will tell you. I will not hold back a word from you.”

verses.rationale: Maintains the self-binding witness formula rather than weakening it to good intentions.
verses.before: They said to Jeremiah, “May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to every word with which the LORD your God sends you to us.
verses.after: They said to Jeremiah, “May the **LORD** be a true and faithful witness against us if we fail to do everything the **LORD** your God sends you to tell us.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to Jeremiah, “May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act according to every word with which the LORD your God sends you to us.

verses.rationale: Renders good or bad as the hearers' reception and preserves the switch to our God.
verses.before: Whether good or bad, we will listen to the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be well with us when we listen to the voice of the LORD our God.”
verses.after: Whether it is welcome or unwelcome, we will obey the **LORD** our God, to whom we are sending you. Then things will go well for us, because we obey the **LORD** our God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whether good or bad, we will listen to the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be well with us when we listen to the voice of the LORD our God.”

verses.rationale: Retains the waiting interval without explanation.
verses.before: At the end of ten days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
verses.after: Ten days later, the word of the **LORD** came to Jeremiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of ten days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.

verses.rationale: Repeats the full audience so the answer matches the request.
verses.before: Then he called Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the armies who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest,
verses.after: He called Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he called Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the armies who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest,

verses.rationale: Links the answer explicitly to their commission.
verses.before: and said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to make your plea fall before him:
verses.after: He told them, “This is what the **LORD**, the God of Israel, says—the one you sent me to with your plea:
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to them, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to make your plea fall before him:

verses.rationale: Preserves building and planting motifs and divine relenting without a doctrinal gloss.
verses.before: If you will truly remain in this land, then I will build you and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I relent concerning the disaster that I have done to you.
verses.after: ‘If you will stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you. For I have relented over the disaster I brought on you.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you will truly remain in this land, then I will build you and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I relent concerning the disaster that I have done to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated prohibition and the hand image.
verses.before: Do not fear the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not fear him,” says the LORD, “for I am with you to save you and to rescue you from his hand.
verses.after: Do not fear the king of Babylon, whom you now fear. Do not fear him, declares the **LORD**, for I am with you to save you and rescue you from his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not fear the king of Babylon, whom you fear. Do not fear him,” says the LORD, “for I am with you to save you and to rescue you from his hand.

verses.rationale: Retains the king as the second agent of mercy and the restoration wording.
verses.before: I will give you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and cause you to return to your own soil.
verses.after: I will grant you mercy, so that he will have mercy on you and restore you to your own ground.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give you compassion, and he will have compassion on you and cause you to return to your own soil.

verses.rationale: Keeps the condition running across verses.
verses.before: “But if you say, ‘We will not remain in this land,’ so that you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God,
verses.after: “But if you say, ‘We will not stay in this land,’ and refuse to obey the **LORD** your God,
verses.tsw_comparator: “But if you say, ‘We will not remain in this land,’ so that you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God,

verses.rationale: Retains all three imagined freedoms as the people's speech.
verses.before: saying, ‘No, but we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the ram’s horn or hunger for bread, and there we will live,’
verses.after: if you say, ‘No! We will go to Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no trumpet, and go hungry for no bread. That is where we will live,’
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, ‘No, but we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the ram’s horn or hunger for bread, and there we will live,’

verses.rationale: Expresses setting the face as determination while retaining the two divine names.
verses.before: then now hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: If you set your faces to enter Egypt and go to live there as resident aliens,
verses.after: then hear the word of the **LORD**, remnant of Judah. This is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘If you are determined to enter Egypt and settle there,
verses.tsw_comparator: then now hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: If you set your faces to enter Egypt and go to live there as resident aliens,

verses.rationale: Preserves the personified pursuit and repeated location.
verses.before: then the sword that you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine that you dread will cling to you there in Egypt, and there you will die.
verses.after: the sword you fear will catch up with you there in Egypt. The famine you dread will cling to you there in Egypt. There you will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the sword that you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine that you dread will cling to you there in Egypt, and there you will die.

verses.rationale: Retains the three threats and paired denial of escape.
verses.before: So it will be with all the people who set their faces to go to Egypt to live there as resident aliens: they will die by sword, famine, and plague. None of them will remain or escape from the disaster that I am bringing upon them.
verses.after: Everyone determined to go and settle in Egypt will die by sword, famine, or plague. No survivor or fugitive will escape the disaster I am bringing on them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: So it will be with all the people who set their faces to go to Egypt to live there as resident aliens: they will die by sword, famine, and plague. None of them will remain or escape from the disaster that I am bringing upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the poured wrath and four consequences, explaining the oath term in context.
verses.before: “For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Just as my anger and fury were poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my fury will be poured out upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become a curse, a horror, a malediction, and a reproach, and you will see this place no more.
verses.after: “For this is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘As my anger and wrath were poured out on Jerusalem's inhabitants, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you enter Egypt. You will become an example invoked in oaths, an object of horror, a curse, and a disgrace. You will never see this place again.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Just as my anger and fury were poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my fury will be poured out upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become a curse, a horror, a malediction, and a reproach, and you will see this place no more.

verses.rationale: Separates Jeremiah's warning from the quoted divine command.
verses.before: The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Know certainly that I have testified against you today.
verses.after: “The **LORD** has spoken to you, remnant of Judah: ‘Do not go to Egypt.’ Be certain of this: I have warned you today.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has spoken concerning you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Know certainly that I have testified against you today.

verses.rationale: Reads the erring as endangering their lives; preserves all three divine names in the recalled pledge.
verses.before: For you have misled yourselves at the cost of your lives, for you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, ‘Pray for us to the LORD our God, and according to all that the LORD our God says, tell us so, and we will do it.’
verses.after: You have made a fatal mistake. You yourselves sent me to the **LORD** your God, saying, ‘Pray for us to the **LORD** our God. Tell us everything the **LORD** our God says, and we will do it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have misled yourselves at the cost of your lives, for you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, ‘Pray for us to the LORD our God, and according to all that the LORD our God says, tell us so, and we will do it.’

verses.rationale: Retains the accusation that their response has already failed the pledge.
verses.before: I have told you today, but you have not listened to the voice of the LORD your God in anything with which he sent me to you.
verses.after: I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the **LORD** your God in anything he sent me to tell you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have told you today, but you have not listened to the voice of the LORD your God in anything with which he sent me to you.

verses.rationale: Closes with the repeated certainty and the place they desire.
verses.before: Now therefore know certainly that you will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where you desire to go to live as resident aliens.”
verses.after: So be certain: you will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where you want to go and settle.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore know certainly that you will die by sword, famine, and plague in the place where you desire to go to live as resident aliens.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated completeness of the message and two divine names.
verses.before: When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God with which the LORD their God had sent him to them—all these words—
verses.after: Jeremiah finished telling all the people every word of the **LORD** their God—all these words the **LORD** their God had sent him to speak to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God with which the LORD their God had sent him to them—all these words—

verses.rationale: Keeps Azariah distinct from 42:1 and the accusation directly in their speech.
verses.before: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, “You are speaking falsehood. The LORD our God did not send you to say, ‘Do not go to Egypt to live there as resident aliens.’
verses.after: Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, “You are lying! The **LORD** our God did not send you to say, ‘Do not go to Egypt to settle there.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, “You are speaking falsehood. The LORD our God did not send you to say, ‘Do not go to Egypt to live there as resident aliens.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the allegation against Baruch without endorsing it as narration.
verses.before: Yet Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us in order to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, so that they may put us to death and carry us into exile to Babylon.”
verses.after: Baruch son of Neriah is turning you against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans so they can kill us or carry us into exile in Babylon.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us in order to give us into the hand of the Chaldeans, so that they may put us to death and carry us into exile to Babylon.”

verses.rationale: Connects the narrator's judgment to the explicit command.
verses.before: So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the armies, and all the people did not listen to the voice of the LORD to remain in the land of Judah.
verses.after: So Johanan son of Kareah, all the army commanders, and all the people refused to obey the **LORD**'s command to stay in the land of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the armies, and all the people did not listen to the voice of the LORD to remain in the land of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the return from dispersion before the renewed displacement.
verses.before: Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been driven to live in the land of Judah:
verses.after: Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders took the whole remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been scattered to settle in Judah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies took all the remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been driven to live in the land of Judah:

verses.rationale: Preserves each group and Jeremiah and Baruch as people taken, not willing leaders.
verses.before: the men, women, little children, the king’s daughters, every person whom Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
verses.after: the men, women, children, and king's daughters—everyone Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan. They also took Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
verses.tsw_comparator: the men, women, little children, the king’s daughters, every person whom Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, and Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the journey and disobedience together.
verses.before: They entered the land of Egypt, for they did not listen to the voice of the LORD, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
verses.after: They entered Egypt, refusing to obey the **LORD**, and reached Tahpanhes.
verses.tsw_comparator: They entered the land of Egypt, for they did not listen to the voice of the LORD, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.

verses.rationale: Retains the new location of revelation.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah at Tahpanhes, saying,
verses.after: In Tahpanhes, the word of the **LORD** came to Jeremiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah at Tahpanhes, saying,

verses.rationale: Uses brickwork for the uncertain installation, with a note, and retains public witnesses.
verses.before: “Take large stones in your hand and hide them in mortar in the pavement at the entrance of Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the Judean men.
verses.after: “Take large stones and hide them in the mortar of the brickwork at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, while the men of Judah watch.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take large stones in your hand and hide them in mortar in the pavement at the entrance of Pharaoh’s palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the Judean men.

verses.rationale: Keeps my servant and the divine first-person action, following the read form of canopy.
verses.before: Say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am sending and taking Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.
verses.after: Tell them, ‘This is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am sending for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will place his throne over these stones I have hidden, and he will spread his canopy above them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am sending and taking Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will set his throne above these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal canopy over them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threefold destiny formula rather than paraphrasing it away.
verses.before: He will come and strike the land of Egypt: those for death, to death; those for captivity, to captivity; and those for the sword, to the sword.
verses.after: He will come and strike Egypt: those destined for death, to death; those for captivity, to captivity; those for the sword, to the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will come and strike the land of Egypt: those for death, to death; those for captivity, to captivity; and those for the sword, to the sword.

verses.rationale: Retains shifts from I to he and the garment image; temples and gods remain linked in the pronouns.
verses.before: I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and carry them captive. He will wrap the land of Egypt around himself as a shepherd wraps his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.
verses.after: I will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods. He will burn them and carry them away. He will wrap himself in Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and leave there unharmed.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will kindle a fire in the houses of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and carry them captive. He will wrap the land of Egypt around himself as a shepherd wraps his garment, and he will go out from there in peace.

verses.rationale: Retains Beth-shemesh and explains its Egyptian setting in a note.
verses.before: He will break the pillars of Beth-Shemesh that is in the land of Egypt and burn the houses of the gods of Egypt with fire.”
verses.after: He will shatter the pillars of Beth-shemesh in Egypt and burn the temples of Egypt's gods.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: He will break the pillars of Beth-Shemesh that is in the land of Egypt and burn the houses of the gods of Egypt with fire.”

verses.rationale: Keeps four locations; Noph is rendered by the established name Memphis.
verses.before: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt, living at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and in the land of Pathros, saying,
verses.after: The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans living in Egypt—in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt, living at Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and in the land of Pathros, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves the audience's witness to the present ruins.
verses.before: “Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You yourselves have seen all the disaster that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah. Look, they are a ruin this day, and no one lives in them,
verses.after: “This is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and all Judah's towns. Today they lie ruined, with no one living in them,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You yourselves have seen all the disaster that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah. Look, they are a ruin this day, and no one lives in them,

verses.rationale: Retains three groups in the unknown-gods formula.
verses.before: because of the evil that they did to provoke me to anger by going to burn incense and serve other gods whom they had not known, neither they, you, nor your ancestors.
verses.after: because of the evil they did to provoke me. They went to burn incense and serve other gods, gods unknown to them, to you, and to your ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of the evil that they did to provoke me to anger by going to burn incense and serve other gods whom they had not known, neither they, you, nor your ancestors.

verses.rationale: Expresses repeated sending naturally and keeps the urgent plea and hatred.
verses.before: Yet I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, ‘Please do not do this detestable thing that I hate.’
verses.after: Again and again I sent you all my servants the prophets, saying, ‘Please do not do this abhorrent thing that I hate.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, saying, ‘Please do not do this detestable thing that I hate.’

verses.rationale: Keeps refusal to listen connected to refusal to turn.
verses.before: But they did not listen or incline their ear to turn from their evil, not burning incense to other gods.
verses.after: But they would not listen or pay attention. They would not turn from their evil and stop burning incense to other gods.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not listen or incline their ear to turn from their evil, not burning incense to other gods.

verses.rationale: Retains the mixed pouring and burning images and present result.
verses.before: So my fury and my anger were poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin and a desolation, as they are this day.
verses.after: So my wrath and anger poured out and burned in Judah's towns and Jerusalem's streets. They became ruins, a desolation, as they are today.
verses.tsw_comparator: So my fury and my anger were poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin and a desolation, as they are this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the extended title and all four threatened groups.
verses.before: “And now, thus says the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel: Why are you doing great evil against your own lives, to cut off from yourselves man and woman, child and nursing infant from the midst of Judah, leaving yourselves no remnant?
verses.after: “Now this is what the **LORD**, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you bringing such great harm on yourselves, cutting off man and woman, child and nursing infant from Judah, leaving yourselves no remnant?
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, thus says the LORD, the God of Hosts, the God of Israel: Why are you doing great evil against your own lives, to cut off from yourselves man and woman, child and nursing infant from the midst of Judah, leaving yourselves no remnant?

verses.rationale: Unpacks the long question while retaining human agency and worldwide disgrace.
verses.before: Why provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live as resident aliens, so that you cut yourselves off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
verses.after: Why provoke me with what your hands have made, burning incense to other gods in Egypt, where you have come to settle? You will cut yourselves off and become a curse and a disgrace among all the nations of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live as resident aliens, so that you cut yourselves off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?

verses.rationale: Retains all responsible groups, resolving the singular possessive collectively with a note.
verses.before: Have you forgotten the evil of your ancestors, the evil of the kings of Judah, the evil of their wives, your own evil, and the evil of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
verses.after: Have you forgotten the evil of your ancestors, of Judah's kings and their wives, of yourselves and your wives, done in Judah and in Jerusalem's streets?
verses.tsw_comparator: Have you forgotten the evil of your ancestors, the evil of the kings of Judah, the evil of their wives, your own evil, and the evil of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

verses.rationale: Keeps the source's third-person shift and instruction language.
verses.before: They have not been humbled to this day, nor have they feared or walked in my instruction and my statutes that I set before you and before your ancestors.
verses.after: To this day they have not humbled themselves or shown reverence. They have not followed my instruction and my statutes, which I set before you and your ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have not been humbled to this day, nor have they feared or walked in my instruction and my statutes that I set before you and before your ancestors.

verses.rationale: Preserves the set-face image corresponding to their determination to go to Egypt.
verses.before: “Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am setting my face against you for harm, to cut off all Judah.
verses.after: “Therefore this is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am setting my face against you for disaster, to cut off all Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am setting my face against you for harm, to cut off all Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated totality and paired means of death without smoothing repetition.
verses.before: I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to live there as resident aliens, and they will all be consumed. In the land of Egypt they will fall; by sword and famine they will be consumed. From least to greatest they will die by sword and famine, and they will become a curse, a horror, a malediction, and a reproach.
verses.after: I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces toward Egypt to settle there, and they will all come to an end in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and waste away in famine. From the least to the greatest, they will die by sword and famine and become an example invoked in oaths, an object of horror, a curse, and a disgrace.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to live there as resident aliens, and they will all be consumed. In the land of Egypt they will fall; by sword and famine they will be consumed. From least to greatest they will die by sword and famine, and they will become a curse, a horror, a malediction, and a reproach.

verses.rationale: Retains the parallel reckoning and full triad.
verses.before: I will attend to people who live in the land of Egypt just as I attended to Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and plague.
verses.after: I will call those living in Egypt to account, just as I called Jerusalem to account, by sword, famine, and plague.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will attend to those who live in the land of Egypt just as I attended to Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and plague.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exception after the sweeping denial instead of harmonizing it away.
verses.before: None of the remnant of Judah who entered the land of Egypt to live there as resident aliens will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, to which they lift up their lives to return and dwell there. They will not return except fugitives.”
verses.after: None of the remnant of Judah who have come to settle in Egypt will escape or survive to return to Judah, where they long to return and live. They will not return—except for a few fugitives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: None of the remnant of Judah who entered the land of Egypt to live there as resident aliens will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, to which they lift up their lives to return and dwell there. They will not return except fugitives.”

verses.rationale: Keeps men's knowledge, women's participation, and the assembly's size.
verses.before: Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women who stood by—a great assembly—and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt in Pathros answered Jeremiah, saying,
verses.after: Then all the men who knew their wives were burning incense to other gods, all the women standing there—a large assembly—and all the people living in Pathros in Egypt answered Jeremiah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women who stood by—a great assembly—and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt in Pathros answered Jeremiah, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains the direct refusal of the named divine message.
verses.before: “As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you.
verses.after: “As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the **LORD**, we will not listen to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “As for the word that you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the people's explanation of past prosperity as their own claim.
verses.before: But we will certainly do every word that has gone out from our mouths, burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of food and were well and saw no disaster.
verses.after: We will certainly do everything we have promised: burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our officials did in Judah's towns and Jerusalem's streets. Then we had plenty of bread, lived well, and saw no disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we will certainly do every word that has gone out from our mouths, burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of food and were well and saw no disaster.

verses.rationale: Retains the contrasting causal account without narrator endorsement.
verses.before: But from the time we ceased burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by sword and famine.”
verses.after: But ever since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and been consumed by sword and famine.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But from the time we ceased burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by sword and famine.”

verses.rationale: Identifies the speakers from our husbands; records the uncertain image-making expression in a note.
verses.before: And the women said, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her in her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands?”
verses.after: The women added, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes bearing her image and pour out offerings without our husbands?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the women said, “When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes for her in her image and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the comprehensive audience for the counterargument.
verses.before: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and to the women and to all the people who had answered him a word, saying,
verses.after: Jeremiah answered all the people—the men, the women, and everyone who had replied to him:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and to the women and to all the people who had answered him a word, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps both rhetorical questions and all participating groups.
verses.before: “The incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—did not the LORD remember it, and did it not come up upon his heart?
verses.after: “The incense you burned in Judah's towns and Jerusalem's streets—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—wasn't that what the **LORD** remembered? Didn't it come to his mind?
verses.tsw_comparator: “The incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—did not the LORD remember it, and did it not come up upon his heart?

verses.rationale: Retains the stated limit of divine endurance and its narrated result.
verses.before: The LORD could no longer bear it because of the evil of your deeds and because of the detestable things you committed. Therefore your land became a ruin, a horror, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is this day.
verses.after: The **LORD** could no longer bear your evil deeds and the abhorrent things you did. That is why your land became a ruin, a horror, and a curse, without inhabitants, as it is today.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD could no longer bear it because of the evil of your deeds and because of the detestable things you committed. Therefore your land became a ruin, a horror, and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine names and three kinds of instruction in the causal conclusion.
verses.before: Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD and did not listen to the voice of the LORD or walk in his instruction, statutes, and testimonies, therefore this disaster has happened to you, as it is this day.”
verses.after: Because you burned incense and sinned against the **LORD**, because you did not obey the **LORD** or follow his instruction, statutes, and testimonies, this disaster has overtaken you, as you see today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD and did not listen to the voice of the LORD or walk in his instruction, statutes, and testimonies, therefore this disaster has happened to you, as it is this day.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the women explicitly addressed before the vow language.
verses.before: Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, “Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women, “Hear the word of the **LORD**, all you people of Judah in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, “Hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains the ironic challenge, repeated vows, and mouth/hand correspondence; notes feminine verb forms.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying, ‘We will surely perform our vows that we vowed, to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.’ Then surely establish your vows and surely perform your vows!
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: ‘You and your wives have carried out with your hands what you said with your mouths: “We will certainly fulfill our vows to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.” Go ahead, confirm your vows! Fulfill your vows!
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying, ‘We will surely perform our vows that we vowed, to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.’ Then surely establish your vows and surely perform your vows!

verses.rationale: Preserves all three divine-name occurrences and the ban on the oath formula.
verses.before: So hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who live in the land of Egypt: Look, I swear by my great name,” says the LORD, “that my name will no longer be called by the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, ‘As the Lord GOD lives.’
verses.after: But hear the word of the **LORD**, all Judah living in Egypt: I swear by my great name, says the **LORD**, that no one from Judah anywhere in Egypt will again invoke my name by saying, “As the Lord **GOD** lives.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all Judah who live in the land of Egypt: Look, I swear by my great name,” says the LORD, “that my name will no longer be called by the mouth of any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, ‘As the Lord GOD lives.’

verses.rationale: Keeps watching turned toward disaster and the repeated completion.
verses.before: Look, I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will be consumed by sword and famine until they are finished.
verses.after: I am watching over them for harm, not for good. All the people of Judah in Egypt will be consumed by sword and famine until they are finished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am watching over them for harm and not for good, and all the men of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will be consumed by sword and famine until they are finished.

verses.rationale: Retains the few survivors and the contest between competing words.
verses.before: But a few in number who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to live there as resident aliens will know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.
verses.after: Only a few who escape the sword will return from Egypt to Judah. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to settle in Egypt will know whose word stands—mine or theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: But a few in number who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah. Then all the remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to live there as resident aliens will know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sign's purpose and repeated standing of words.
verses.before: “And this will be the sign for you,” says the LORD, “that I am attending to you in this place, so that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for harm:
verses.after: And this will be your sign, declares the **LORD**, that I will call you to account in this place, so you may know that my words of disaster against you will certainly stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And this will be the sign for you,” says the LORD, “that I am attending to you in this place, so that you may know that my words will surely stand against you for harm:

verses.rationale: Preserves the two kings' parallel fates and the named Pharaoh.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of people who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.”
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: I am handing Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: Look, I am giving Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies and into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.”

verses.rationale: Makes dictation and the earlier date explicit without rearranging the book.
verses.before: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in a book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
verses.after: This is the word Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when Baruch wrote these words on a scroll as Jeremiah dictated them, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in a book from the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:

verses.rationale: Retains the personally addressed oracle.
verses.before: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:
verses.after: “This is what the **LORD**, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:

verses.rationale: Keeps Baruch's lament and attribution of added grief to God.
verses.before: You said, ‘Woe to me! For the LORD has added grief to my pain. I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.’
verses.after: ‘You said, “Woe to me! The **LORD** has added grief to my pain. I am worn out with groaning and can find no rest.”’
verses.tsw_comparator: You said, ‘Woe to me! For the LORD has added grief to my pain. I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the message-within-message and building/planting motifs.
verses.before: “Thus you will say to him: Thus says the LORD: Look, what I built I am tearing down, and what I planted I am uprooting— that is, this whole land.
verses.after: “This is what you are to tell him: ‘The **LORD** says: What I built, I am tearing down; what I planted, I am uprooting— and that means the whole land.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus you shall say to him: Thus says the LORD: Look, what I built I am tearing down, and what I planted I am uprooting— that is, this whole land.

verses.rationale: Retains all flesh and the recurring life-as-plunder image without inventing Baruch's ambitions.
verses.before: And you—do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For look, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh,” says the LORD, “but I will give you your life as plunder in every place where you go.”
verses.after: And you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. I am bringing disaster on all flesh, declares the **LORD**. But wherever you go, I will give you your life as plunder.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And you—do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For look, I am bringing disaster upon all flesh,” says the LORD, “but I will give you your life as plunder in every place where you go.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the collection heading as a verse.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations:
verses.after: The word of the **LORD** that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations:

verses.rationale: Preserves the full battle location, rulers, and regnal date.
verses.before: Concerning Egypt, concerning the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
verses.after: Concerning Egypt: the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates at Carchemish and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Egypt, concerning the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the shield terms and retains the martial summons.
verses.before: Prepare shield and buckler, and draw near for battle!
verses.after: “Ready the small shield and the large shield! Advance to battle!
verses.tsw_comparator: Prepare shield and buckler, and draw near for battle!

verses.rationale: Keeps the sequence of equipment and preparation commands.
verses.before: Harness the horses and mount, riders! Take your stand with helmets; polish the spears; put on the coats of armor!
verses.after: Harness the horses! Mount up, riders! Take your positions with helmets on. Polish the spears; put on your armor!
verses.tsw_comparator: Harness the horses and mount, riders! Take your stand with helmets; polish the spears; put on the coats of armor!

verses.rationale: Retains the sudden reversal and familiar terror refrain.
verses.before: Why do I see it? They are terrified; they are turning backward. Their warriors are beaten down and flee in haste without looking back. Terror is all around, says the LORD.
verses.after: Why do I see them terrified, falling back? Their warriors are crushed. They flee in panic and do not look back. Terror on every side!” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do I see it? They are terrified; they are turning backward. Their warriors are beaten down and flee in haste without looking back. Terror is all around, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Reads the prohibitive forms as the impossibility of escape in the defeat scene.
verses.before: The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape. In the north, by the bank of the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.
verses.after: The swift cannot flee; the warrior cannot escape. In the north, beside the Euphrates, they stumble and fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape. In the north, by the bank of the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.

verses.rationale: Keeps the identifying question and rising-water image.
verses.before: Who is this rising like the Nile, whose waters surge like rivers?
verses.after: Who is this rising like the Nile, whose waters surge like rivers?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who is this rising like the Nile, whose waters surge like rivers?

verses.rationale: Preserves Egypt's boast in its own voice and the repeated river image.
verses.before: Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters surge like rivers. It says, “I will rise; I will cover the earth. I will destroy city and people who live in it.”
verses.after: Egypt rises like the Nile, its waters surging like rivers. It says, “I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy cities and their people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters surge like rivers. It says, “I will rise; I will cover the earth. I will destroy city and those who live in it.”

verses.rationale: Retains the named military peoples and their weapons.
verses.before: Go up, horses! Rage, chariots! Let the warriors go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield, and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.
verses.after: Charge, horses! Race wildly, chariots! Let the warriors march out: Cush and Put, carrying shields, and the Ludim, handling and drawing the bow.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go up, horses! Rage, chariots! Let the warriors go out: Cush and Put, who handle the shield, and the Ludim, who handle and bend the bow.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated divine title, sword's appetite, and sacrificial violence.
verses.before: But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satisfied; it will drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord GOD of Hosts has a sacrifice in the land of the north by the Euphrates River.
verses.after: But that day belongs to the Lord **GOD** of hosts, a day of vengeance, when he takes vengeance on his enemies. The sword will eat its fill and drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord **GOD** of hosts has a sacrifice in the north, beside the Euphrates.
verses.tsw_comparator: But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his adversaries. The sword will devour and be satisfied; it will drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord GOD of Hosts has a sacrifice in the land of the north by the Euphrates River.

verses.rationale: Preserves the personified daughter and fruitless treatment, following the feminine read form.
verses.before: Go up to Gilead and take balm, virgin daughter Egypt. In vain you multiply medicines; there is no healing for you.
verses.after: Go up to Gilead and get balm, virgin daughter Egypt! You multiply remedies in vain; there is no healing for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go up to Gilead and take balm, virgin daughter Egypt. In vain you multiply medicines; there is no healing for you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the linked falls and international hearing.
verses.before: The nations have heard your shame, and your cry has filled the earth, for warrior stumbled against warrior; both of them fell together.
verses.after: The nations have heard of your disgrace; your cry fills the earth. Warrior stumbles over warrior; both fall together.
verses.tsw_comparator: The nations have heard your shame, and your cry has filled the earth, for warrior stumbled against warrior; both of them fell together.

verses.rationale: Marks a new oracle without merging it with the Carchemish heading.
verses.before: The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
verses.after: The word the **LORD** spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon coming to strike Egypt:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:

verses.rationale: Preserves all three local announcements and the sword's consuming action.
verses.before: Declare in Egypt, make it heard in Migdol; make it heard in Memphis and in Tahpanhes. Say: “Take your stand and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured all around you.
verses.after: “Announce it in Egypt; proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes: ‘Take your position and get ready, for the sword has devoured all around you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Declare in Egypt, make it heard in Migdol; make it heard in Memphis and in Tahpanhes. Say: “Take your stand and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured all around you.

verses.rationale: Retains the singular verbs despite the difficult noun form and flags the mighty one in a note.
verses.before: Why has your mighty one been swept away? He did not stand, because the LORD thrust him down.
verses.after: Why is your mighty one swept away? He cannot stand, for the **LORD** has driven him down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why has your mighty one been swept away? He did not stand, because the LORD thrust him down.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine causation and the foreign soldiers' return speech.
verses.before: He made many stumble; indeed, one fell against another. They said, ‘Rise, and let us return to our people and to the land of our birth because of the sword of the oppressor.’
verses.after: He makes many stumble; one falls against another. They say, ‘Get up! Let us return to our people, to the land of our birth, away from the oppressor's sword.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He made many stumble; indeed, one fell against another. They said, ‘Rise, and let us return to our people and to the land of our birth because of the sword of the oppressor.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the taunting title and missed time without supplying a specific deadline.
verses.before: There they called Pharaoh king of Egypt, ‘Noise—he has let the appointed time pass.’
verses.after: There they cry, ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt is all noise! He has let the appointed time pass.’
verses.tsw_comparator: There they called Pharaoh king of Egypt, ‘Noise—he has let the appointed time pass.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the royal oath and two mountain comparisons without naming the figure beyond the context.
verses.before: As I live,” says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, “surely like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea, so he will come.
verses.after: As I live,” declares the King, whose name is the **LORD** of hosts, “one is coming, like Tabor among the mountains, like Carmel beside the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: As I live,” says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, “surely like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea, so he will come.

verses.rationale: Retains exile preparations and personification.
verses.before: Prepare baggage for exile, inhabitant daughter Egypt, for Memphis will become a desolation, burned and without inhabitant.
verses.after: Pack your belongings for exile, daughter dwelling in Egypt! Memphis will become a desolation, laid waste, with no one living there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Prepare baggage for exile, inhabitant daughter Egypt, for Memphis will become a desolation, burned and without inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Uses the biting-insect reading with uncertainty noted and preserves the doubled arrival.
verses.before: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north has come—has come.
verses.after: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a biting fly comes from the north—it comes!
verses.tsw_comparator: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north has come—has come.

verses.rationale: Extends the cattle image to mercenaries and retains both time clauses.
verses.before: Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves, but they also have turned; they have fled together. They did not stand, for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their visitation.
verses.after: Even the hired soldiers among her are like fattened calves. They too turn and flee together; they do not stand. Their day of disaster has come upon them, the time of their reckoning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves, but they also have turned; they have fled together. They did not stand, for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their visitation.

verses.rationale: Keeps the movement of the snake-like sound and the invaders' woodcutting image.
verses.before: Her sound is like a serpent moving away, for they come with an army; with axes they come against her like woodcutters.
verses.after: Her sound retreats like a snake, for they advance in force. They come at her with axes, like men cutting wood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her sound is like a serpent moving away, for they come with an army; with axes they come against her like woodcutters.

verses.rationale: Retains the unsearchable forest and innumerable attackers without rationalizing the metaphors.
verses.before: They will cut down her forest, says the LORD, though it cannot be searched out, for they are more numerous than locusts and without number.
verses.after: They will cut down her forest,” declares the **LORD**, “though it cannot be searched through. They are more numerous than locusts, beyond counting.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will cut down her forest, says the LORD, though it cannot be searched out, for they are more numerous than locusts and without number.

verses.rationale: Keeps the daughter image and transfer into another people's hand.
verses.before: Daughter Egypt is put to shame; she is given into the hand of a people from the north.
verses.after: Daughter Egypt is disgraced, handed over to a people from the north.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Daughter Egypt is put to shame; she is given into the hand of a people from the north.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated Pharaoh and the deity Amon; uses established Thebes for No.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Look, I am attending to Amon of Thebes, Pharaoh, Egypt, her gods and her kings—Pharaoh and people who trust in him.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says, “I am calling Amon of Thebes to account, along with Pharaoh, Egypt, her gods and kings—Pharaoh and everyone who trusts in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Look, I am attending to Amon of Thebes, Pharaoh, Egypt, her gods and her kings—Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

verses.rationale: Keeps both the handing over and the later restoration of habitation.
verses.before: I will give them into the hand of people who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of his servants. Afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I will hand them over to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. Afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in former days,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of his servants. Afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shift to Israel and recurring rescue language.
verses.before: “But you, my servant Jacob, do not fear, and do not be dismayed, Israel. For look, I am saving you from far away and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, and no one will make him afraid.
verses.after: “But you, my servant Jacob, do not fear; do not be dismayed, Israel. I will save you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and live quietly, at ease, with no one to make him afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But you, my servant Jacob, do not fear, and do not be dismayed, Israel. For look, I am saving you from far away and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, and no one will make him afraid.

verses.rationale: Maintains the tension between preservation and punishment without minimizing either.
verses.before: You, my servant Jacob, do not fear,” says the LORD, “for I am with you. Though I make a complete end of all the nations where I drove you, of you I will not make a complete end. I will discipline you in justice, but I will certainly not leave you unpunished.”
verses.after: Do not fear, my servant Jacob,” declares the **LORD**, “for I am with you. I will make an end of all the nations where I have driven you, but I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you justly; I will certainly not leave you unpunished.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You, my servant Jacob, do not fear,” says the LORD, “for I am with you. Though I make a complete end of all the nations where I drove you, of you I will not make a complete end. I will discipline you in justice, but I will certainly not leave you unpunished.”

verses.rationale: Retains the relative historical marker without assigning a date.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:
verses.after: The word of the **LORD** that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:

verses.rationale: Keeps the invading flood and its comprehensive reach.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Look, waters are rising from the north and will become an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and all that fills it, the city and people who live in it. Humanity will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “Look! Waters rise from the north and become an overflowing torrent. They flood the land and everything in it, the towns and those who live there. People cry out; everyone in the land wails.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Look, waters are rising from the north and will become an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and all that fills it, the city and those who live in it. Humanity will cry out, and every inhabitant of the land will wail.

verses.rationale: Preserves the fathers' failure in terror without excusing or softening it.
verses.before: At the sound of the stamping hooves of his stallions, at the rushing of his chariots, at the roar of his wheels, fathers do not turn back for their children, because their hands have become weak,
verses.after: At the pounding hooves of his stallions, the crash of his chariots, the roar of his wheels, fathers do not turn back for their children; their hands hang limp.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of the stamping hooves of his stallions, at the rushing of his chariots, at the roar of his wheels, fathers do not turn back for their children, because their hands have become weak,

verses.rationale: Keeps the named allies and origin without asserting a modern identification.
verses.before: because of the day that is coming to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every remaining helper. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
verses.after: For the day is coming to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off every surviving helper from Tyre and Sidon. The **LORD** is destroying the Philistines, the remnant from the coastland of Caphtor.
verses.tsw_comparator: because of the day that is coming to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every remaining helper. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned valley wording and preserves mourning self-injury.
verses.before: Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?
verses.after: Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. Remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?
verses.tsw_comparator: Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you cut yourself?

verses.rationale: Retains direct appeal to the personified sword.
verses.before: Ah, sword of the LORD! How long until you are quiet? Gather yourself into your sheath; rest and be still!
verses.after: Alas, sword of the **LORD**! How long before you rest? Return to your sheath; be still and silent!
verses.tsw_comparator: Ah, sword of the LORD! How long until you are quiet? Gather yourself into your sheath; rest and be still!

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from addressing the sword to speaking about it.
verses.before: How can it be quiet when the LORD has commanded it? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast— there he has appointed it.”
verses.after: How can you rest, when the **LORD** has commanded it? Against Ashkelon and the seacoast— there he has assigned it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: How can it be quiet when the LORD has commanded it? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast— there he has appointed it.”

verses.rationale: Uses stronghold for the ambiguous Misgab term, noting the possible place name.
verses.before: Concerning Moab. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Woe to Nebo, for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame and captured; the stronghold is put to shame and shattered.
verses.after: Concerning Moab. This is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo, for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is disgraced and captured; the stronghold is disgraced and shattered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Moab. Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Woe to Nebo, for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame and captured; the stronghold is put to shame and shattered.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named town Madmen and the planning/silence wordplays in notes.
verses.before: The praise of Moab is no more. In Heshbon they have devised evil against her: ‘Come, let us cut her off from being a nation.’ You also, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will go after you.
verses.after: Moab's praise is gone. In Heshbon they plan her ruin: ‘Come, let us wipe her out as a nation.’ You too, Madmen, will fall silent; the sword will pursue you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The praise of Moab is no more. In Heshbon they have devised evil against her: ‘Come, let us cut her off from being a nation.’ You also, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will go after you.

verses.rationale: Retains the abrupt reported cry.
verses.before: A sound of crying from Horonaim: devastation and great breaking!
verses.after: A cry sounds from Horonaim: ‘Devastation! Great destruction!’
verses.tsw_comparator: A sound of crying from Horonaim: devastation and great breaking!
