verses.rationale: Follows the read form little ones instead of adopting the alternative place-name reading.
verses.before: Moab is broken; her little ones make their cry heard.
verses.after: Moab is broken; her little ones raise a cry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab is broken; her little ones make their cry heard.

verses.rationale: Preserves uphill/downhill geography and doubled weeping; notes difficult anguish phrase.
verses.before: For on the ascent to Luhith weeping goes up with weeping, and on the descent to Horonaim they hear the distressing cry of breaking.
verses.after: Up the slope to Luhith they go weeping, weeping. On the descent from Horonaim they hear anguished cries of destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: For on the ascent to Luhith weeping goes up with weeping, and on the descent to Horonaim they hear the distressing cry of breaking.

verses.rationale: Uses the shrub reading and leaves the alternative wild-donkey interpretation in a note.
verses.before: Flee! Save your lives! Become like a shrub in the wilderness.
verses.after: Flee! Save your lives! Be like a shrub in the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flee! Save your lives! Become like a shrub in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Keeps works unspecific and follows read forms for Chemosh and together.
verses.before: For because you trusted in your works and in your treasures, you also will be captured. Chemosh will go out into exile, his priests and his officials together.
verses.after: Because you trusted in your works and treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into exile, his priests and officials together.
verses.tsw_comparator: For because you trusted in your works and in your treasures, you also will be captured. Chemosh will go out into exile, his priests and his officials together.

verses.rationale: Preserves the every/none repetition and two landscapes.
verses.before: The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will perish, and the plain will be destroyed, as the LORD has spoken.
verses.after: A destroyer will come to every town; not one town will escape. The valley will perish and the plateau be destroyed, as the **LORD** has said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will perish, and the plain will be destroyed, as the LORD has spoken.

verses.rationale: Chooses the wings/flight reading of two difficult words and explicitly notes uncertainty.
verses.before: Give wings to Moab, for she will surely fly away. Her cities will become a desolation, without anyone living in them.
verses.after: Give Moab wings, for she must fly away. Her towns will become a desolation, with no one living in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give wings to Moab, for she will surely fly away. Her cities will become a desolation, without anyone living in them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the violent curse intact and tied to the oracle rather than generalizing it.
verses.before: Cursed is the one who does the work of the LORD negligently, and cursed is the one who keeps the sword from blood.
verses.after: Cursed is the one who does the **LORD**'s work carelessly; cursed is the one who holds his sword back from blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cursed is the one who does the work of the LORD negligently, and cursed is the one who keeps the sword from blood.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sustained wine-making image and its explanation by exile.
verses.before: Moab has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs. He has not been poured from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. So his taste remains in him, and his scent has not changed.
verses.after: Moab has been at ease since youth, settled on its lees. It has not been poured from vessel to vessel or gone into exile. So its flavor remains and its aroma has not changed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs. He has not been poured from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. Therefore his taste remains in him, and his scent has not changed.

verses.rationale: Repeats tipping and retains vessel destruction.
verses.before: So look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will send pourers to him, and they will pour him out. They will empty his vessels and smash his jars.
verses.after: Therefore days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when I will send people to tip it out. They will tip it out, empty its vessels, and smash its jars.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will send pourers to him, and they will pour him out. They will empty his vessels and smash his jars.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparison between Moab's deity and Israel's trusted sanctuary.
verses.before: Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence.
verses.after: Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, the place it trusted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their confidence.

verses.rationale: Preserves the challenge to military self-description.
verses.before: How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men for battle’?
verses.after: How can you say, ‘We are warriors, men strong in battle’?
verses.tsw_comparator: How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men for battle’?

verses.rationale: Supplies attacker as the implied subject of the difficult ascent clause and retains up/down movement.
verses.before: Moab is devastated, and they have gone up against her cities. Her choice young men have gone down to slaughter,” says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: Moab is devastated; an attacker has gone up against its towns. Its finest young men go down to slaughter,” declares the King, whose name is the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab is devastated, and they have gone up against her cities. Her choice young men have gone down to slaughter,” says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the twofold imminence.
verses.before: The disaster of Moab is near to come, and her calamity hurries greatly.
verses.after: Moab's disaster is near; its calamity is coming swiftly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The disaster of Moab is near to come, and her calamity hurries greatly.

verses.rationale: Retains the staff and rod images of power.
verses.before: Mourn for her, all you who are around her, everyone who know her name. Say, ‘How the strong staff is broken, the beautiful rod!’
verses.after: Mourn for it, all you neighbors, all who know its name. Say, “How the mighty staff is broken, the splendid rod!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Mourn for her, all you who are around her, all who know her name. Say, ‘How the strong staff is broken, the beautiful rod!’

verses.rationale: Follows the read imperative and keeps the unusual thirst image.
verses.before: Come down from glory and sit in thirst, inhabitant daughter Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has destroyed your strongholds.
verses.after: Come down from your glory; sit in thirst, daughter dwelling in Dibon. Moab's destroyer has come against you; he has ruined your fortifications.
verses.tsw_comparator: Come down from glory and sit in thirst, inhabitant daughter Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has destroyed your strongholds.

verses.rationale: Makes both masculine and feminine fugitives visible.
verses.before: Stand by the road and watch, inhabitant of Aroer. Ask the fleeing man and the escaping woman; say, ‘What has happened?’
verses.after: Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer. Ask the fleeing man and escaping woman, “What has happened?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Stand by the road and watch, inhabitant of Aroer. Ask the fleeing man and the escaping woman; say, ‘What has happened?’

verses.rationale: Keeps the cry's answer and the announcement's location.
verses.before: Moab is put to shame, for she is broken. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is devastated.
verses.after: “Moab is disgraced, for it is shattered! Wail and cry out! Announce beside the Arnon that Moab is devastated.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab is put to shame, for she is broken. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is devastated.

verses.rationale: Retains the opening of the place list and read form Mephaath.
verses.before: Judgment has come upon the land of the plain: upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath;
verses.after: Judgment has come to the plateau—to Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
verses.tsw_comparator: Judgment has come upon the land of the plain: upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath;

verses.rationale: Preserves all three names without shortening the list.
verses.before: upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-Diblathaim;
verses.after: to Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
verses.tsw_comparator: upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-Diblathaim;

verses.rationale: Maintains the continued list and consistent Kiriathaim spelling.
verses.before: upon Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, and Beth-Meon;
verses.after: to Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
verses.tsw_comparator: upon Kiriathaim, Beth-Gamul, and Beth-Meon;

verses.rationale: Retains the list's comprehensive far/near close.
verses.before: upon Kerioth and Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
verses.after: to Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the towns of Moab, far and near.
verses.tsw_comparator: upon Kerioth and Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.

verses.rationale: Preserves both bodily images of defeated strength.
verses.before: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,” says the LORD.
verses.after: “Moab's horn is cut off; its arm is broken,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps degrading bodily language and the too that connects the next verse.
verses.before: “Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the LORD. Moab will wallow in his vomit, and he also will become a laughingstock.
verses.after: “Make it drunk, for it has made itself great against the **LORD**. Moab will wallow in its vomit and become a laughingstock too.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the LORD. Moab will wallow in his vomit, and he also will become a laughingstock.

verses.rationale: Preserves the questions and gesture of contempt without answering them.
verses.before: Was Israel not a laughingstock to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you shook your head?
verses.after: Wasn't Israel a laughingstock to you? Was Israel found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of it you shook your head?
verses.tsw_comparator: Was Israel not a laughingstock to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you shook your head?

verses.rationale: Retains the refuge command and exposed nesting image.
verses.before: Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, inhabitants of Moab. Be like a dove that nests on the sides of the mouth of a gorge.
verses.after: Leave your towns and live among the rocks, people of Moab. Be like a dove that nests at the mouth of a ravine.
verses.tsw_comparator: Leave the cities and dwell in the rock, inhabitants of Moab. Be like a dove that nests on the sides of the mouth of a gorge.

verses.rationale: Retains the deliberate accumulation of pride terms.
verses.before: We have heard of the pride of Moab— he is exceedingly proud— his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.
verses.after: We have heard of Moab's pride— so very proud! Its loftiness, its pride, its arrogance, its haughty heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have heard of the pride of Moab— he is exceedingly proud— his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated nothing-result while noting the difficult boasts clause.
verses.before: “I know his fury,” says the LORD, “but his boasts are false; his deeds are false.
verses.after: I know its fury,” declares the **LORD**, “but it amounts to nothing. Its empty boasts accomplish nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I know his fury,” says the LORD, “but his boasts are false; his deeds are false.

verses.rationale: Preserves first-person lament and the impersonal third-person final verb.
verses.before: So I will wail over Moab; for all Moab I will cry out. For the people of Kir-Heres they will moan.
verses.after: So I wail for Moab; I cry out for all Moab. There is mourning for the people of Kir-heres.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will wail over Moab; for all Moab I will cry out. For the people of Kir-Heres they will moan.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult sea of Jazer wording and extended vine geography.
verses.before: More than the weeping for Jazer I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea; they reached as far as Jazer. The destroyer has fallen upon your summer fruit and upon your grape harvest.
verses.after: More than the weeping for Jazer, I weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea, reaching the sea of Jazer. A destroyer has fallen on your summer fruit and your grape harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: More than the weeping for Jazer I will weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your branches crossed the sea; they reached as far as Jazer. The destroyer has fallen upon your summer fruit and upon your grape harvest.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated shout as its meaning changes.
verses.before: Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab. I have caused wine to cease from the presses; no one treads with the shout of joy. The shouting will not be a shout of joy.
verses.after: Joy and gladness are taken from the orchards and the land of Moab. I have stopped the wine in the presses. No one treads grapes with a joyful shout; the shouting is no shout of joy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab. I have caused wine to cease from the presses; no one treads with the shout of joy. The shouting will not be a shout of joy.

verses.rationale: Retains the geographical spread and Eglath as an uncertain place name.
verses.before: From the cry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, they have raised their voice; from Zoar as far as Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. For even the waters of Nimrim will become desolate.
verses.after: From Heshbon to Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, their cries ring out; from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah. Even the waters of Nimrim have become desolate.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the cry of Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz, they have raised their voice; from Zoar as far as Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. For even the waters of Nimrim will become desolate.

verses.rationale: Keeps the cultic actions and the declared termination.
verses.before: “I will cause to cease in Moab,” says the LORD, “the one who offers on the high place and the one who burns incense to his gods.
verses.after: “I will put an end in Moab,” declares the **LORD**, “to those who offer on the high place and burn incense to their gods.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will cause to cease in Moab,” says the LORD, “the one who offers on the high place and the one who burns incense to his gods.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated heart and musical mourning image without assigning the speaker beyond context.
verses.before: So my heart moans for Moab like flutes, and my heart moans like flutes for the people of Kir-Heres. So the abundance they acquired has perished.
verses.after: So my heart sounds like pipes for Moab; my heart sounds like pipes for the people of Kir-heres. The wealth they gained has perished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore my heart moans for Moab like flutes, and my heart moans like flutes for the people of Kir-Heres. Therefore the abundance they acquired has perished.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive mourning and physical injury.
verses.before: For every head is bald, and every beard is clipped. On all hands are cuts, and sackcloth is on the waist.
verses.after: Every head is shaved, every beard cut off. Every hand is gashed, every waist wrapped in sackcloth.
verses.tsw_comparator: For every head is bald, and every beard is clipped. On all hands are cuts, and sackcloth is on the waist.

verses.rationale: Keeps the rejected-vessel image and the divine explanation.
verses.before: On all the roofs of Moab and in its public squares there is lamentation, for I have broken Moab like a vessel no one desires,” says the LORD.
verses.after: On every rooftop of Moab and in all its squares, nothing but mourning! “For I have broken Moab like a vessel no one wants,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: On all the roofs of Moab and in its public squares there is lamentation, for I have broken Moab like a vessel no one desires,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the exclamations and twofold effect on surrounding peoples.
verses.before: “How she is broken! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and a terror to all around him.”
verses.after: How it is shattered! Wail! How Moab has turned its back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and a terror to all its neighbors.
verses.tsw_comparator: “How she is broken! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and a terror to all around him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the invader unnamed within the eagle comparison.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “Look, one will fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “Look! One swoops like an eagle, spreading his wings over Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “Look, one will fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Moab.

verses.rationale: Uses towns with Kerioth alternative noted; preserves the comparison's gendered image.
verses.before: The cities are captured, and the strongholds are seized. The heart of Moab’s warriors on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
verses.after: The towns are captured; the strongholds seized. On that day Moab's warriors will have hearts like a woman in labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities are captured, and the strongholds are seized. The heart of Moab’s warriors on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor.

verses.rationale: Repeats the source's reason for judgment.
verses.before: Moab will be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the LORD.
verses.after: Moab will be destroyed as a people, for it made itself great against the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moab will be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three dangers and notes their Hebrew sound pattern.
verses.before: Terror and pit and snare are upon you, inhabitant of Moab,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Terror, pit, and trap await you, inhabitant of Moab,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Terror and pit and snare are upon you, inhabitant of Moab,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the inescapable sequence and follows the read participle.
verses.before: “The one who flees from the terror will fall into the pit; the one who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of their visitation,” says the LORD.
verses.after: “Whoever flees the terror falls into the pit; whoever climbs from the pit is caught in the trap. For I will bring upon Moab the year of its reckoning,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The one who flees from the terror will fall into the pit; the one who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of their visitation,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily geography and earlier conquest echo without replacing the unusual imagery.
verses.before: “In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand without strength, for fire has gone out from Heshbon and flame from the midst of Sihon. It has devoured the forehead of Moab and the crown of the sons of tumult.
verses.after: In Heshbon's shadow the fugitives stand exhausted. But fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's midst. It consumes Moab's forehead, the crown of the noisy people's head.
verses.tsw_comparator: “In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand without strength, for fire has gone out from Heshbon and flame from the midst of Sihon. It has devoured the forehead of Moab and the crown of the sons of tumult.

verses.rationale: Retains the parallel sons/daughters and repeated captivity.
verses.before: Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken captive and your daughters into captivity.
verses.after: Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished. Your sons are taken captive, your daughters into captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken captive and your daughters into captivity.

verses.rationale: Keeps the restoration promise and editorial closing formula distinct.
verses.before: Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days,” says the LORD. Thus far is the judgment on Moab.
verses.after: “Yet in days to come I will restore Moab's fortunes,” declares the **LORD**. Here ends the judgment on Moab.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days,” says the LORD. Thus far is the judgment on Moab.

verses.rationale: Uses Milcom with the their king alternative noted, preserving the inheritance questions.
verses.before: Concerning the children of Ammon. Thus says the LORD: “Does Israel have no sons? Does he have no heir? Why then has Milcom possessed Gad, and his people lived in its cities?
verses.after: Concerning the Ammonites. This is what the **LORD** says: “Has Israel no sons? Has it no heir? Why has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and why do his people live in Gad's towns?
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning the children of Ammon. Thus says the LORD: “Does Israel have no sons? Does he have no heir? Why then has Milcom possessed Gad, and his people lived in its cities?

verses.rationale: Keeps the reversal of possession and both divine names.
verses.before: So look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will make the sound of the battle cry heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon. It will become a desolate mound, and its daughter towns will be burned with fire. Then Israel will possess people who possessed him,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Therefore days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a desolate mound; its surrounding towns will be burned. Then Israel will dispossess those who dispossessed it,” says the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will make the sound of the battle cry heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon. It will become a desolate mound, and its daughter towns will be burned with fire. Then Israel will possess those who possessed him,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the uncertain Ai and enclosures without modern identification.
verses.before: “Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth; lament, and run back and forth among the walls, for Milcom will go into exile, his priests and his officials together.
verses.after: “Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, mourn, and wander among the enclosures. Milcom is going into exile, his priests and officials together.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth; lament, and run back and forth among the walls, for Milcom will go into exile, his priests and his officials together.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult flowing-valley phrase and the daughter's boast, noting uncertainty.
verses.before: Why do you boast in the valleys, your flowing valley, backsliding daughter, who trusts in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come against me?’
verses.after: Why boast about your valleys, your flowing valley, faithless daughter? You trust in your treasures and say, ‘Who will come against me?’
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you boast in the valleys, your flowing valley, backsliding daughter, who trusts in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come against me?’

verses.rationale: Retains scattering without a rescuer and the full divine title.
verses.before: Look, I am bringing terror upon you,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts, “from all those around you. You will be driven out, each straight ahead, and no one will gather the fugitives.
verses.after: I am bringing terror on you from all around,” declares the Lord **GOD** of hosts. “Each of you will be driven straight ahead, with no one to gather the wanderers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am bringing terror upon you,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts, “from all those around you. You will be driven out, each straight ahead, and no one will gather the fugitives.

verses.rationale: Keeps restoration after judgment without expanding the timing.
verses.before: But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the children of Ammon,” says the LORD.
verses.after: But afterward I will restore the Ammonites' fortunes,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the children of Ammon,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves three questions and the decay image; notes discerning/sons ambiguity.
verses.before: Concerning Edom. Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the discerning? Has their wisdom decayed?
verses.after: Concerning Edom. This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Is there no wisdom left in Teman? Has counsel vanished from the discerning? Has their wisdom decayed?
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Edom. Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the discerning? Has their wisdom decayed?

verses.rationale: Keeps Dedan addressed and Esau named as the object of reckoning.
verses.before: Flee! Turn back! Dwell deep, inhabitants of Dedan, for I will bring the disaster of Esau upon him at the time I attend to him.
verses.after: Flee! Turn away! Hide deep, people of Dedan. For I bring Esau's disaster upon him, the time when I call him to account.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flee! Turn back! Dwell deep, inhabitants of Dedan, for I will bring the disaster of Esau upon him at the time I attend to him.

verses.rationale: Retains the comparison of limited ordinary plundering with the following exposure.
verses.before: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not destroy only enough for themselves?
verses.after: If grape pickers came to you, wouldn't they leave gleanings? If thieves came at night, they would destroy only as much as they wanted.
verses.tsw_comparator: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not destroy only enough for themselves?

verses.rationale: Preserves the expanding circle of devastation and final disappearance.
verses.before: Yet I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he cannot conceal himself. His offspring are destroyed, and his brothers and his neighbors, and he is no more.
verses.after: But I have stripped Esau bare, exposed his hiding places; he cannot hide. His offspring, relatives, and neighbors are devastated, and he is no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he cannot conceal himself. His offspring are destroyed, and his brothers and his neighbors, and he is no more.

verses.rationale: Keeps the surprising promise intact without making it ironic by assertion.
verses.before: Leave your orphans; I will preserve them alive, and let your widows trust in me.”
verses.after: Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Leave your orphans; I will preserve them alive, and let your widows trust in me.”

verses.rationale: Retains the cup and repeated certainty rather than supplying an explanation of comparative guilt.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD: “Look, those whose judgment was not to drink the cup must surely drink. And you—will you go entirely unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but you will surely drink.
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** says: “Those who were not sentenced to drink the cup must drink it. Will you go entirely unpunished? You will not go unpunished; you must drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD: “Look, those whose judgment was not to drink the cup must surely drink. And you—will you go entirely unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but you shall surely drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves the divine self-oath and four consequences.
verses.before: For I have sworn by myself,” says the LORD, “that Bozrah will become a horror, a reproach, a ruin, and a curse, and all its cities will become everlasting ruins.”
verses.after: For I swear by myself,” declares the **LORD**, “Bozrah will become a horror, a disgrace, a ruin, and a curse. All its towns will be lasting ruins.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have sworn by myself,” says the LORD, “that Bozrah will become a horror, a reproach, a ruin, and a curse, and all its cities will become everlasting ruins.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the report and messenger's summons distinct.
verses.before: I have heard a report from the LORD, and a messenger has been sent among the nations: “Gather yourselves and come against her! Rise for battle!”
verses.after: I have heard a report from the **LORD**; a messenger is sent among the nations: “Gather and come against her! Rise up for battle!”
verses.tsw_comparator: I have heard a report from the LORD, and a messenger has been sent among the nations: “Gather yourselves and come against her! Rise for battle!”

verses.rationale: Retains the reversal from feared power to low status.
verses.before: For look, I have made you small among the nations, despised among humanity.
verses.after: “I have made you small among the nations, despised among humankind.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I have made you small among the nations, despised among humanity.

verses.rationale: Keeps feared reputation, rocky setting, and high-nest reversal.
verses.before: The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, from there I will bring you down,” says the LORD.
verses.after: The terror you inspire has deceived you, along with the arrogance of your heart. You live in clefts of the rock and occupy the hilltops. Though you make your nest high as an eagle's, from there I will bring you down,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, from there I will bring you down,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the response and wound image.
verses.before: “Edom will become a horror. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and hiss because of all its wounds.
verses.after: Edom will become a horror. Everyone passing by will be appalled and hiss at all its wounds.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Edom will become a horror. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and hiss because of all its wounds.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full comparison and paired denial of habitation.
verses.before: As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will live there, and no human being will stay in it.
verses.after: “As when Sodom, Gomorrah, and their neighbors were overthrown,” says the **LORD**, “no one will live there; no human being will settle there.
verses.tsw_comparator: As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will live there, and no human being will stay in it.

verses.rationale: Maintains lion/pasture/shepherd imagery and successive questions; notes disputed pronouns.
verses.before: “Look, like a lion coming up from the pride of the Jordan against an enduring pasture, so suddenly I will make him run away from her. And whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. For who is like me? Who will summon me? And what shepherd can stand before me?
verses.after: Look! Like a lion he comes up from the Jordan's thickets against a lasting pasture. In a moment I will drive him away from it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? Who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, like a lion coming up from the pride of the Jordan against an enduring pasture, so suddenly I will make him run away from her. And whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. For who is like me? Who will summon me? And what shepherd can stand before me?

verses.rationale: Keeps the smallest sheep as the dragged objects and renders the causative desolation of their pasture; alternative syntax noted.
verses.before: So hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counseled against Edom, and his purposes that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely they will drag away the little ones of the flock; surely he will make their pasture desolate over them.
verses.after: So hear the **LORD**'s plan against Edom, what he has devised against Teman's inhabitants: Even the smallest of the flock will be dragged away; he will lay their pasture waste because of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counseled against Edom, and his purposes that he has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely they will drag away the little ones of the flock; surely he will make their pasture desolate over them.

verses.rationale: Retains the geographical reach and literal sea name.
verses.before: At the sound of their fall the earth trembles; their cry— its sound is heard at the Sea of Reeds.
verses.after: At the sound of their fall the earth shakes; their cry is heard at the Sea of Reeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of their fall the earth trembles; their cry— its sound is heard at the Sea of Reeds.

verses.rationale: Maintains the parallel with Moab's oracle and the same gendered image.
verses.before: Look, one will rise and fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah. The heart of Edom’s warriors on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor.”
verses.after: Look! One rises and swoops like an eagle, spreading his wings over Bozrah. On that day Edom's warriors will have hearts like a woman in labor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, one will rise and fly like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah. The heart of Edom’s warriors on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned sea wording rather than silently emending it to hearts.
verses.before: Concerning Damascus. “Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They melt in fear; there is anxiety like the sea that cannot be quiet.
verses.after: Concerning Damascus. “Hamath and Arpad are shamed; they have heard bad news and melt away. Anxiety stirs the sea; it cannot be still.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Damascus. “Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They melt in fear; there is anxiety like the sea that cannot be quiet.

verses.rationale: Preserves the city as female and accumulating labor distress.
verses.before: Damascus has become weak; she turns to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pains have taken hold of her like a woman giving birth.
verses.after: Damascus has grown weak and turned to flee. Trembling grips her; distress and pangs seize her like a woman giving birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Damascus has become weak; she turns to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pains have taken hold of her like a woman giving birth.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult negative and first-person delight; note gives uncertainty.
verses.before: How has the city of praise not been abandoned, the city of my joy?
verses.after: How is the city of praise not abandoned, the town of my delight?
verses.tsw_comparator: How has the city of praise not been abandoned, the city of my joy?

verses.rationale: Keeps young men and combatants distinct and silencing as death imagery.
verses.before: So her young men will fall in her public squares, and all the men of war will be silenced on that day,” says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: Therefore her young men will fall in her squares; all her fighting men will be silenced that day,” declares the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore her young men will fall in her public squares, and all the men of war will be silenced on that day,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named dynasty and fire's movement from wall to palaces.
verses.before: “I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will consume the palaces of Ben-Hadad.”
verses.after: “I will set fire to Damascus's wall, and it will consume Ben-hadad's palaces.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will consume the palaces of Ben-Hadad.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the plural kingdoms and the source's Nebuchadnezzar read form.
verses.before: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus says the LORD: “Rise, go up against Kedar; destroy the children of the east!
verses.after: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. This is what the **LORD** says: “Rise up! Advance against Kedar; devastate the people of the east.
verses.tsw_comparator: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck. Thus says the LORD: “Rise, go up against Kedar; destroy the children of the east!

verses.rationale: Retains the pastoral possessions and the recurring terror formula.
verses.before: Their tents and their flocks they will take; their curtains and all their vessels and their camels they will carry away. They will cry to them, ‘Terror is all around!’
verses.after: Take their tents and flocks, their tent curtains and all their equipment. Carry off their camels, and cry out over them, ‘Terror on every side!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Their tents and their flocks they will take; their curtains and all their vessels and their camels they will carry away. They will cry to them, ‘Terror is all around!’

verses.rationale: Follows the read second-person suffix and preserves plan/scheme parallelism.
verses.before: Flee! Wander far away! Dwell deep, inhabitants of Hazor,” says the LORD, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has counseled counsel against you and purposed a purpose against you.
verses.after: Flee far away! Hide deep, people of Hazor,” declares the **LORD**. “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has planned against you; he has devised a scheme against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flee! Wander far away! Dwell deep, inhabitants of Hazor,” says the LORD, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has counseled counsel against you and purposed a purpose against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the vulnerability of an unfortified, isolated people without endorsing the attack.
verses.before: Rise, go up against a nation at ease, living securely,” says the LORD, “which has neither gates nor bars and dwells alone.
verses.after: Rise up! Advance against a nation at ease, living securely,” declares the **LORD**, “with neither gates nor bars, dwelling apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rise, go up against a nation at ease, living securely,” says the LORD, “which has neither gates nor bars and dwells alone.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hair custom rather than generalizing it to a geographical group.
verses.before: Their camels will become plunder, and the multitude of their livestock spoil. I will scatter to every wind people who clip the corners of their hair, and from every side I will bring their disaster,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Their camels will become booty, their many herds plunder. I will scatter to every wind those who clip the edges of their hair. From every side I will bring their disaster,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their camels will become plunder, and the multitude of their livestock spoil. I will scatter to every wind those who clip the corners of their hair, and from every side I will bring their disaster,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated habitation formula and animal inhabitants.
verses.before: “Hazor will become a dwelling for jackals, a desolation forever. No one will live there, and no human being will stay in it.”
verses.after: “Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a desolation forever. No one will live there; no human being will settle there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hazor will become a dwelling for jackals, a desolation forever. No one will live there, and no human being will stay in it.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the earlier date in this collection's present order.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
verses.after: The word of the **LORD** that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:

verses.rationale: Preserves the weapon as the chief expression of power.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Look, I am breaking the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “I am breaking Elam's bow, the mainstay of its strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Look, I am breaking the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.

verses.rationale: Keeps four repeated and follows the read Elam rather than the written form's ambiguity.
verses.before: I will bring upon Elam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation to which the outcasts of Elam will not come.
verses.after: I will bring four winds against Elam from the four ends of the heavens. I will scatter its people to all these winds; there will be no nation where Elam's outcasts do not arrive.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring upon Elam four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation to which the outcasts of Elam will not come.

verses.rationale: Retains the pursuing sword and comprehensive threat.
verses.before: I will make Elam terrified before their enemies and before people who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger,” says the LORD. “I will send the sword after them until I have consumed them.
verses.after: I will shatter Elam before its enemies, before those who seek its life. I will bring disaster upon them, my burning anger,” declares the **LORD**. “I will send the sword after them until I have finished them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make Elam terrified before their enemies and before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger,” says the LORD. “I will send the sword after them until I have consumed them.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine rule replacing the local rulers.
verses.before: I will set my throne in Elam and destroy from there king and officials,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I will set my throne in Elam and destroy its king and officials,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will set my throne in Elam and destroy from there king and officials,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows both read forms and preserves restoration after the threat of an end.
verses.before: “But it will be in the latter days that I will restore the fortunes of Elam,” says the LORD.
verses.after: “Yet in days to come I will restore Elam's fortunes,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But it will be in the latter days that I will restore the fortunes of Elam,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named land and mediation by Jeremiah.
verses.before: The word that the LORD spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet:
verses.after: The word the **LORD** spoke concerning Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that the LORD spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet:

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated commands and paired disgrace/shattering of named gods and images.
verses.before: “Declare among the nations and make it heard; lift up a banner and make it heard. Do not conceal it. Say: ‘Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered. Her images are put to shame; her idols are shattered.
verses.after: “Announce it among the nations; proclaim it! Raise a signal flag; proclaim it, hide nothing! Say, ‘Babylon is captured! Bel is disgraced; Merodach is shattered. Her images are disgraced; her idols are shattered.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Declare among the nations and make it heard; lift up a banner and make it heard. Do not conceal it. Say: ‘Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered. Her images are put to shame; her idols are shattered.

verses.rationale: Preserves direction and the flight of both humans and animals.
verses.before: For a nation is coming up against her from the north. It will make her land a desolation, and no one will live in it. From human to animal, they have fled; they have gone away.’
verses.after: A nation has come against her from the north. It will turn her land into a desolation, with no one living there. People and animals alike have fled and gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a nation is coming up against her from the north. It will make her land a desolation, and no one will live in it. From human to animal, they have fled; they have gone away.’

verses.rationale: Retains the joined peoples, ongoing weeping, and repeated divine name.
verses.before: “In those days and at that time,” says the LORD, “the children of Israel will come, they and the children of Judah together. They will go along weeping as they go, and they will seek the LORD their God.
verses.after: In those days, at that time,” declares the **LORD**, “the people of Israel and Judah will come together. They will walk along weeping and seek the **LORD** their God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “In those days and at that time,” says the LORD, “the children of Israel will come, they and the children of Judah together. They will go along weeping as they go, and they will seek the LORD their God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the directional posture and the people's covenant invitation.
verses.before: They will ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned toward it: ‘Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.’
verses.after: They will ask the way to Zion, their faces turned toward her: ‘Come, let us join ourselves to the **LORD** in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.’
verses.tsw_comparator: They will ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned toward it: ‘Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.’

verses.rationale: Follows the read plural forms and sustains the sheep image.
verses.before: “My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray; they turned them loose on the mountains. From mountain to hill they went; they forgot their resting place.
verses.after: My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray, turning them loose on the mountains. They wandered from mountain to hill and forgot their resting place.
verses.tsw_comparator: “My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray; they turned them loose on the mountains. From mountain to hill they went; they forgot their resting place.

verses.rationale: Preserves the enemies' self-excuse as quoted speech, with both divine names and pasture title.
verses.before: Everyone who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said, ‘We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, the habitation of righteousness, the LORD, the hope of their ancestors.’
verses.after: Everyone who found them devoured them. Their enemies said, ‘We are not guilty, because they sinned against the **LORD**, the pasture of righteousness, the **LORD**, the hope of their ancestors.’
verses.tsw_comparator: All who found them devoured them, and their adversaries said, ‘We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, the habitation of righteousness, the LORD, the hope of their ancestors.’

verses.rationale: Follows the read imperative and keeps the leading-goat comparison.
verses.before: “Flee from the midst of Babylon; go out from the land of the Chaldeans. Be like male goats before the flock.
verses.after: Flee from Babylon; leave the land of the Chaldeans. Be like male goats at the head of the flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Flee from the midst of Babylon; go out from the land of the Chaldeans. Be like male goats before the flock.

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual arrow/warrior comparison and assured result.
verses.before: For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will arrange themselves against her; from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like those of a skilled warrior; none returns empty.
verses.after: I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the north. They will line up against her; from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like a skilled warrior who does not return empty-handed.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will arrange themselves against her; from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like those of a skilled warrior; none returns empty.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated plunder and satiation.
verses.before: Chaldea will become plunder; everyone who plunder her will be satisfied,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will have their fill,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Chaldea will become plunder; all who plunder her will be satisfied,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows read plural addresses and retains both animal images.
verses.before: “Though you rejoice, though you exult, you who plunder my inheritance, though you frolic like a heifer in grass and neigh like stallions,
verses.after: “Though you rejoice and exult, you who pillage my inheritance, though you frisk like a heifer threshing grain and neigh like stallions,
verses.tsw_comparator: “Though you rejoice, though you exult, you who plunder my inheritance, though you frolic like a heifer in grass and neigh like stallions,

verses.rationale: Preserves motherland personification and the three landscape terms.
verses.before: your mother will be greatly put to shame; she who bore you will be humiliated. Look, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
verses.after: your mother will be deeply ashamed; the one who bore you will be disgraced. Look! She is last among the nations— a wilderness, a dry and barren land.
verses.tsw_comparator: your mother will be greatly put to shame; she who bore you will be humiliated. Look, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.

verses.rationale: Keeps the wounds and onlookers' reaction.
verses.before: Because of the wrath of the LORD she will not be inhabited but will become entirely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be horrified and hiss because of all her wounds.
verses.after: Because of the **LORD**'s wrath, no one will live there; she will be wholly desolate. Everyone passing Babylon will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of the wrath of the LORD she will not be inhabited but will become entirely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be horrified and hiss because of all her wounds.

verses.rationale: Preserves the commands and stated reason without toning down the assault.
verses.before: “Arrange yourselves against Babylon all around, everyone who bend the bow. Shoot at her; do not spare arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.
verses.after: Take your positions all around Babylon, all you who draw the bow. Shoot at her; spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Arrange yourselves against Babylon all around, all who bend the bow. Shoot at her; do not spare arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Explains the hand gesture while retaining it and the repeated vengeance language.
verses.before: Shout against her all around! She has given her hand; her pillars have fallen, her walls are torn down. For this is the vengeance of the LORD. Take vengeance upon her; as she has done, do to her.
verses.after: Raise the battle cry against her on every side! She has given her hand in surrender. Her foundations have fallen; her walls are torn down. This is the **LORD**'s vengeance. Take vengeance on her; do to her what she has done.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shout against her all around! She has given her hand; her pillars have fallen, her walls are torn down. For this is the vengeance of the LORD. Take vengeance upon her; as she has done, do to her.

verses.rationale: Keeps the attack on agriculture and the dispersal of foreign inhabitants.
verses.before: Cut off the sower from Babylon and the one who handles the sickle at harvest time. Because of the sword of the oppressor, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.
verses.after: Cut off the sower from Babylon and the one who wields the sickle at harvest. Before the oppressor's sword, each will turn to their own people; each will flee to their own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Cut off the sower from Babylon and the one who handles the sickle at harvest time. Because of the sword of the oppressor, each will turn to his own people, and each will flee to his own land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sequential predators and the intensified bone image.
verses.before: “Israel is a scattered sheep; lions drove him away. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now, last, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has crushed his bones.
verses.after: Israel is a scattered sheep driven away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured it; now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has gnawed its bones.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Israel is a scattered sheep; lions drove him away. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now, last, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has crushed his bones.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comparison between imperial reckonings.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am attending to the king of Babylon and to his land as I attended to the king of Assyria.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: “I will call the king of Babylon and his land to account, as I called the king of Assyria to account.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Look, I am attending to the king of Babylon and to his land as I attended to the king of Assyria.

verses.rationale: Maintains the sheep image and all four grazing regions.
verses.before: I will bring Israel back to his pasture. He will feed on Carmel and Bashan, and on the hill country of Ephraim and Gilead his life will be satisfied.
verses.after: I will bring Israel back to its pasture. It will graze on Carmel and Bashan; in Ephraim's hills and Gilead it will have its fill.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring Israel back to his pasture. He will feed on Carmel and Bashan, and on the hill country of Ephraim and Gilead his life will be satisfied.

verses.rationale: Preserves the search and absence explained by forgiveness.
verses.before: In those days and at that time,” says the LORD, “the guilt of Israel will be sought, but there will be none, and the sins of Judah, but they will not be found, for I will forgive those whom I leave as a remnant.
verses.after: In those days, at that time,” declares the **LORD**, “Israel's guilt will be sought, but there will be none; Judah's sins will not be found. For I will forgive those I leave as a remnant.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days and at that time,” says the LORD, “the guilt of Israel will be sought, but there will be none, and the sins of Judah, but they will not be found, for I will forgive those whom I leave as a remnant.

verses.rationale: Retains charged place names and the destruction ban, explained without endorsement in notes.
verses.before: “Go up against the land of Merathaim and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Strike and devote to destruction after them,” says the LORD, “and do according to all that I have commanded you.
verses.after: Advance against the land of Merathaim and the inhabitants of Pekod. Pursue them with the sword; devote them to destruction,” declares the **LORD**. “Do everything I have commanded you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go up against the land of Merathaim and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Strike and devote to destruction after them,” says the LORD, “and do according to all that I have commanded you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the abrupt sound report.
verses.before: A sound of battle is in the land, and great breaking!
verses.after: The sound of battle in the land! Great destruction!
verses.tsw_comparator: A sound of battle is in the land, and great breaking!

verses.rationale: Keeps the empire-as-hammer image and repeated exclamation.
verses.before: How the hammer of the entire earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
verses.after: How the hammer of the whole earth has been cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
verses.tsw_comparator: How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!

verses.rationale: Preserves the trap and unawareness, with the divine name in the reason clause.
verses.before: I laid a snare for you, and you were caught, Babylon, but you did not know it. You were found and seized because you contended against the LORD.
verses.after: I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught without knowing it. You were found and seized, for you challenged the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: I laid a snare for you, and you were caught, Babylon, but you did not know it. You were found and seized because you contended against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps both divine names and martial storehouse imagery.
verses.before: The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his fury, for the Lord GOD of Hosts has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
verses.after: The **LORD** has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his wrath. The Lord **GOD** of hosts has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his fury, for the Lord GOD of Hosts has a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.

verses.rationale: Retains the harvest/storage images and absolute destruction command.
verses.before: “Come against her from the farthest end. Open her storehouses. Pile her up like heaps and devote her to destruction. Let no remnant be left to her.
verses.after: Come against her from every side. Open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain. Devote her to destruction; leave her no remnant.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Come against her from the farthest end. Open her storehouses. Pile her up like heaps and devote her to destruction. Let no remnant be left to her.

verses.rationale: Preserves bulls as the oracle's image rather than replacing them with a military explanation.
verses.before: Slaughter all her bulls; let them go down to slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their visitation.
verses.after: Slaughter all her bulls; let them go down to the killing place. Woe to them! Their day has come, the time of their reckoning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Slaughter all her bulls; let them go down to slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their visitation.

verses.rationale: Keeps the survivors' announcement and temple focus.
verses.before: A sound of people who flee and escape from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for his temple.
verses.after: Listen! Fugitives and survivors from the land of Babylon announce in Zion the vengeance of the **LORD** our God, vengeance for his temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: A sound of those who flee and escape from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for his temple.

verses.rationale: Follows the supplementary read pronoun and preserves repayment repetitions.
verses.before: “Call archers against Babylon, everyone who bend the bow. Camp against her all around; let no one escape. Repay her according to her work; according to all she has done, do to her, for she acted proudly against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: Summon archers against Babylon, all who draw the bow. Camp all around her; let no one escape. Repay her for her deeds; do to her everything she has done. For she has acted arrogantly against the **LORD**, against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Call archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow. Camp against her all around; let no one escape. Repay her according to her work; according to all she has done, do to her, for she acted proudly against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the echo of the Damascus oracle.
verses.before: So her young men will fall in her public squares, and all her men of war will be silenced on that day,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her fighting men will be silenced that day,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore her young men will fall in her public squares, and all her men of war will be silenced on that day,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Treats arrogance as a personified address rather than silently adding a nation name.
verses.before: “Look, I am against you, O Pride,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts, “for your day has come, the time when I attend to you.
verses.after: “I am against you, Arrogance,” declares the Lord **GOD** of hosts. “Your day has come, the time when I call you to account.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, I am against you, O Pride,” says the Lord GOD of Hosts, “for your day has come, the time when I attend to you.

verses.rationale: Maintains the personification and fall without recovery.
verses.before: Pride will stumble and fall, and no one will raise him up. I will kindle fire in his cities, and it will consume all around him.”
verses.after: Arrogance will stumble and fall, with no one to raise it. I will set its towns on fire, and the fire will consume everything around it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pride will stumble and fall, and no one will raise him up. I will kindle fire in his cities, and it will consume all around him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both peoples and the captors' active refusal.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The children of Israel are oppressed, and the children of Judah with them. Everyone who took them captive hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “The people of Israel and Judah are oppressed together. All their captors hold them fast and refuse to release them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The children of Israel are oppressed, and the children of Judah with them. All who took them captive hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.

verses.rationale: Preserves the legal dispute and rest/trembling contrast.
verses.before: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is his name. He will surely plead their case so that he may give rest to the earth and make the inhabitants of Babylon tremble.
verses.after: Their Redeemer is strong; the **LORD** of hosts is his name. He will vigorously plead their case, to give the earth rest and make Babylon's inhabitants tremble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is his name. He will surely plead their case so that he may give rest to the earth and make the inhabitants of Babylon tremble.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sword refrain and named social groups.
verses.before: “A sword against the Chaldeans,” says the LORD, “and against the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and against her wise men!
verses.after: A sword against the Chaldeans,” declares the **LORD**, “against Babylon's inhabitants, her officials and her wise men!
verses.tsw_comparator: “A sword against the Chaldeans,” says the LORD, “and against the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and against her wise men!

verses.rationale: Renders the boastful liars in their divinatory context and preserves parallel imperatives.
verses.before: A sword against the boasters, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be terrified!
verses.after: A sword against the false diviners— let them become fools! A sword against her warriors— let them be shattered!
verses.tsw_comparator: A sword against the boasters, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be terrified!

verses.rationale: Retains the ancient gendered taunt explicitly, with a note rather than replacing it with weakness.
verses.before: A sword against their horses and against their chariots, and against all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
verses.after: A sword against her horses and chariots, against all the mixed troops within her— they will become women! A sword against her treasures— let them be plundered!
verses.tsw_comparator: A sword against their horses and against their chariots, and against all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!

verses.rationale: Keeps drought as the source's vowel distinction within the sword wordplay.
verses.before: A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and they act madly over terrors.
verses.after: A drought against her waters— let them dry up! For this is a land of carved images, and they go mad over their fearsome idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of carved images, and they act madly over terrors.

verses.rationale: Avoids overprecise identification of the first two animal terms and keeps the duration.
verses.before: So desert creatures will live there with jackals, and daughters of the ostrich will live in her. She will never again be inhabited, nor lived in from generation to generation.
verses.after: So desert creatures and howling animals will live there, and ostriches will make their home there. It will never again be inhabited, never settled from generation to generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore desert creatures will live there with jackals, and daughters of the ostrich will live in her. She will never again be inhabited, nor lived in from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Preserves both God and **LORD** and the repeated Edom comparison.
verses.before: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will live there, and no human being will stay in her.
verses.after: As when God overthrew Sodom, Gomorrah, and their neighbors,” declares the **LORD**, “no one will live there; no human being will settle there.
verses.tsw_comparator: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will live there, and no human being will stay in her.

verses.rationale: Keeps the singular people with plural allied kings.
verses.before: “Look, a people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.
verses.after: “Look! A people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings stirred up from the ends of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, a people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves cruelty, sea sound, organized force, and daughter address.
verses.before: They grasp bow and javelin; they are cruel and have no compassion. Their sound roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, arranged like a man for battle against you, daughter Babylon.
verses.after: They grasp bow and javelin. They are cruel and show no mercy. Their sound roars like the sea; they ride on horses, arrayed as one for battle against you, daughter Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: They grasp bow and javelin; they are cruel and have no compassion. Their sound roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, arranged like a man for battle against you, daughter Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the king's bodily fear and labor comparison.
verses.before: The king of Babylon heard the report of them, and his hands became weak. Distress seized him, pain like a woman giving birth.
verses.after: Babylon's king hears the report, and his hands go limp. Distress grips him, pain like a woman giving birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Babylon heard the report of them, and his hands became weak. Distress seized him, pain like a woman giving birth.

verses.rationale: Preserves third-person arrival then divine first person and matches the Edom refrain without resolving every pronoun.
verses.before: “Look, like a lion coming up from the pride of the Jordan against an enduring pasture, so suddenly I will make them run away from her. And whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. For who is like me? Who will summon me? And what shepherd can stand before me?
verses.after: Look! Like a lion he comes up from the Jordan's thickets against a lasting pasture. In a moment I will drive them away from it. Who is the chosen one I will appoint over it? Who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, like a lion coming up from the pride of the Jordan against an enduring pasture, so suddenly I will make them run away from her. And whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. For who is like me? Who will summon me? And what shepherd can stand before me?

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated flock image and the slight wording difference from 49:20.
verses.before: So hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counseled against Babylon, and his purposes that he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely they will drag away the little ones of the flock; surely he will make their pasture desolate over them.
verses.after: So hear the **LORD**'s plan against Babylon, what he has devised against the land of the Chaldeans: Even the smallest of the flock will be dragged away; he will lay the pasture waste because of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD that he has counseled against Babylon, and his purposes that he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely they will drag away the little ones of the flock; surely he will make their pasture desolate over them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the worldwide response as the oracle closes.
verses.before: At the sound, “Babylon is captured!” the earth trembles, and the cry is heard among the nations.
verses.after: At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth shakes; a cry is heard among the nations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound, “Babylon is captured!” the earth trembles, and the cry is heard among the nations.

verses.rationale: Keeps the coded place name and wind/spirit possibility in a note.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: “Look, I am stirring up against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-Kamai a destroying wind.
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** says: “I am stirring up a destroying wind against Babylon and the people of Leb-kamai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: “Look, I am stirring up against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Leb-Kamai a destroying wind.

verses.rationale: Retains strangers and the winnowing verb, noting the sound play.
verses.before: I will send winnowers to Babylon, and they will winnow her and empty her land, for on the day of disaster they will be against her from every side.
verses.after: I will send strangers against Babylon; they will winnow her and empty her land. They will surround her on the day of disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will send winnowers to Babylon, and they will winnow her and empty her land, for on the day of disaster they will be against her from every side.

verses.rationale: Uses the against reading of the difficult repeated consonants and documents the prohibitive alternative.
verses.before: Against the one who bends the bow let the archer bend his bow, and against the one who rises in his coat of armor. Do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction.
verses.after: Let the archer draw against the one who draws his bow, against the one who rises in armor. Do not spare her young men; devote her whole army to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Against the one who bends the bow let the archer bend his bow, and against the one who rises in his coat of armor. Do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily injury and both locations.
verses.before: They will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, pierced through in her streets.
verses.after: They will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, pierced through in her streets.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, pierced through in her streets.

verses.rationale: Keeps widowing imagery and the disputed their-land referent visible in a note.
verses.before: For Israel is not forsaken, nor Judah, by his God, by the LORD of Hosts, though their land is filled with guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, the **LORD** of hosts, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Israel is not forsaken, nor Judah, by his God, by the LORD of Hosts, though their land is filled with guilt against the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the urgent individual escape and guilt/recompense link.
verses.before: Flee from the midst of Babylon! Each one save his life! Do not be silenced in her guilt, for this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; he is repaying her recompense.
verses.after: Flee from Babylon! Save your lives, each of you. Do not perish in her guilt. This is the **LORD**'s time for vengeance; he is repaying her what she deserves.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flee from the midst of Babylon! Each one save his life! Do not be silenced in her guilt, for this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; he is repaying her recompense.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency and the repeated nations within the cup image.
verses.before: Babylon was a golden cup in the hand of the LORD, making all the earth drunk. The nations drank from her wine; so the nations went mad.
verses.after: Babylon was a golden cup in the **LORD**'s hand, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; that is why the nations went mad.
verses.tsw_comparator: Babylon was a golden cup in the hand of the LORD, making all the earth drunk. The nations drank from her wine; therefore the nations went mad.

verses.rationale: Keeps the tentative healing invitation rather than turning it immediately into certainty of failure.
verses.before: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is broken. Wail over her! Take balm for her pain; perhaps she may be healed.
verses.after: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and shattered! Wail for her. Bring balm for her wound; perhaps she can be healed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is broken. Wail over her! Take balm for her pain; perhaps she may be healed.

verses.rationale: Follows the read verb and keeps the speakers' failed healing and departure.
verses.before: “We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed. Abandon her, and let each of us go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens and is lifted to the skies.
verses.after: ‘We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed. Leave her! Let each of us go to our own land. Her judgment reaches heaven, rises to the clouds.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed. Abandon her, and let each of us go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens and is lifted to the skies.

verses.rationale: Retains plural communal vindication and both divine names.
verses.before: The LORD has brought forth our righteousness. Come, let us recount in Zion the work of the LORD our God.”
verses.after: The **LORD** has brought our vindication to light. Come, let us tell in Zion what the **LORD** our God has done.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has brought forth our righteousness. Come, let us recount in Zion the work of the LORD our God.”

verses.rationale: Uses shields with equipment uncertainty noted; preserves Media and temple vengeance.
verses.before: Sharpen the arrows; fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her. For this is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance for his temple.
verses.after: Polish the arrows! Take up the shields! The **LORD** has stirred the spirit of the kings of Media. His purpose is to destroy Babylon. This is the **LORD**'s vengeance, vengeance for his temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sharpen the arrows; fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her. For this is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance for his temple.

verses.rationale: Keeps the accumulation of military commands and planned/accomplished pairing.
verses.before: Lift up a banner against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the guard; set the watchmen; prepare the ambushes. For the LORD has both purposed and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
verses.after: Raise a signal against Babylon's walls. Strengthen the watch; post sentries; prepare the ambush. The **LORD** has both planned and carried out what he said against Babylon's inhabitants.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up a banner against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the guard; set the watchmen; prepare the ambushes. For the LORD has both purposed and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the ambiguous measure/gain expression and explains a possible life-thread reading in a note.
