verses.before: You who dwell by many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your gain.
verses.after: You who dwell beside many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come— the measure of your gain.
verses.tsw_comparator: You who dwell by many waters, abundant in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your gain.

verses.rationale: Keeps the oath, insect comparison, and shout.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts has sworn by himself: “Surely I will fill you with people like locusts, and they will raise a shout against you.”
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts has sworn by himself: ‘I will fill you with men like locusts, and they will raise a victory shout over you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts has sworn by himself: “Surely I will fill you with people like locusts, and they will raise a shout against you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the three creation clauses and distinct faculties.
verses.before: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.
verses.after: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains the weather sequence and storehouse image.
verses.before: At the sound of his voice there is a roar of waters in the heavens. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain and brings wind from his storehouses.
verses.after: When he gives voice, waters roar in heaven. He raises clouds from the ends of the earth, makes lightning for the rain, and brings wind from his storehouses.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the sound of his voice there is a roar of waters in the heavens. He makes clouds rise from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning for the rain and brings wind from his storehouses.

verses.rationale: Keeps the craft criticism, singular/plural shift, and absence of breath.
verses.before: Every human being is senseless, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by the carved image, for his cast image is falsehood and there is no breath in them.
verses.after: Everyone is senseless, without knowledge; every metalworker is ashamed of the carved image. The cast image is a lie; there is no breath in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every human being is senseless, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by the carved image, for his cast image is falsehood and there is no breath in them.

verses.rationale: Retains vapor rather than replacing the image solely with worthlessness.
verses.before: They are emptiness, a work of mockery; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
verses.after: They are vapor, a work of delusion; at the time of their reckoning they will perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: They are emptiness, a work of mockery; at the time of their visitation they will perish.

verses.rationale: Does not silently insert Israel where this verse omits it; note explains the implicit tribe.
verses.before: The portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the one who formed everything, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD of Hosts is his name.
verses.after: Jacob's Portion is not like these. He is the one who forms all things, and the tribe is his inheritance. The **LORD** of hosts is his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the one who formed everything, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD of Hosts is his name.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unnamed instrument and ongoing-action rendering consistently through the repeated clauses.
verses.before: “You are my war club, my weapons of war. With you I shatter nations; with you I destroy kingdoms.
verses.after: “You are my war club, my weapon of battle. With you I shatter nations; with you I destroy kingdoms.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You are my war club, my weapons of war. With you I shatter nations; with you I destroy kingdoms.

verses.rationale: Retains both repetitions and paired military targets.
verses.before: With you I shatter horse and rider; with you I shatter chariot and rider.
verses.after: With you I shatter horse and rider; with you I shatter chariot and driver.
verses.tsw_comparator: With you I shatter horse and rider; with you I shatter chariot and rider.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated violence against all specified groups, including noncombatants.
verses.before: With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter old and young; with you I shatter young man and young woman.
verses.after: With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter old and young; with you I shatter young man and virgin.
verses.tsw_comparator: With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter old and young; with you I shatter young man and young woman.

verses.rationale: Keeps occupational pairs and the final officials without collapsing the list.
verses.before: With you I shatter shepherd and flock; with you I shatter farmer and team; with you I shatter governors and officials.
verses.after: With you I shatter shepherd and flock; with you I shatter farmer and team; with you I shatter governors and deputies.
verses.tsw_comparator: With you I shatter shepherd and flock; with you I shatter farmer and team; with you I shatter governors and officials.

verses.rationale: Keeps the before-your-eyes phrase without silently resolving which event it modifies.
verses.before: Yet I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all their evil that they did in Zion before your eyes,” says the LORD.
verses.after: I will repay Babylon and all who live in Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion, before your eyes,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all their evil that they did in Zion before your eyes,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves Babylon as mountain despite its literal geography.
verses.before: “Look, I am against you, O destroying mountain,” says the LORD, “you who destroy all the earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the cliffs, and make you a burned-out mountain.
verses.after: “I am against you, destroying mountain,” declares the **LORD**, “you who destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the crags, and make you a burned-out mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Look, I am against you, O destroying mountain,” says the LORD, “you who destroy all the earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the cliffs, and make you a burned-out mountain.

verses.rationale: Retains the two rejected building uses and permanent ruin.
verses.before: They will not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for a foundation, for you will become everlasting desolations,” says the LORD.
verses.after: No one will take from you a cornerstone or a stone for foundations. You will be a lasting desolation,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for a foundation, for you will become everlasting desolations,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves consecration, three kingdoms, and the bristling insect image.
verses.before: Lift up a banner in the land! Blow the ram’s horn among the nations! Consecrate nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts.
verses.after: Raise a signal in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Consecrate nations against her; summon kingdoms against her— Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lift up a banner in the land! Blow the ram’s horn among the nations! Consecrate nations against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated consecration and complete administrative reach; smooths collective pronouns minimally.
verses.before: Consecrate nations against her— the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the land of their rule.
verses.after: Consecrate nations against her: the kings of Media, its governors and all its deputies, and every land under their rule.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consecrate nations against her— the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the land of their rule.

verses.rationale: Keeps earth's labor-like response and the standing plan.
verses.before: The earth trembles and writhes, for the purposes of the LORD stand against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.
verses.after: The earth shakes and writhes, for the **LORD**'s purposes against Babylon stand: to make Babylon's land a desolation, with no one living there.
verses.tsw_comparator: The earth trembles and writhes, for the purposes of the LORD stand against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon a desolation without inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Retains the ancient gendered taunt, explained in notes, alongside concrete military collapse.
verses.before: The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting; they remain in their strongholds. Their strength has dried up; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.
verses.after: Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting. They stay in their strongholds; their strength has failed; they have become women. Her homes are set on fire; her gate bars are broken.
verses.tsw_comparator: The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting; they remain in their strongholds. Their strength has dried up; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; her bars are broken.

verses.rationale: Preserves the rushing repeated messengers and comprehensive capture reading.
verses.before: Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from every side.
verses.after: Runner meets runner, messenger meets messenger, to tell Babylon's king that his city is captured from end to end.
verses.tsw_comparator: Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from every side.

verses.rationale: Keeps marshes rather than silently substituting boats or fortifications.
verses.before: The crossings are seized, the marshes are burned with fire, and the men of war are terrified.
verses.after: The crossings are seized, the marshes burned with fire, and the fighting men terrified.
verses.tsw_comparator: The crossings are seized, the marshes are burned with fire, and the men of war are terrified.

verses.rationale: Preserves threshing and harvest order as the image presents it.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden down. Yet a little while, and the time of harvest will come for her.”
verses.after: For this is what the **LORD** of hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. A little longer, and her harvest time will come.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: “Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden down. Yet a little while, and the time of harvest will come for her.”

verses.rationale: Follows singular read forms and keeps all bodily and vessel images.
verses.before: “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me and crushed me; he made me an empty vessel. Like a sea monster he swallowed me; he filled his belly with my delicacies and cast me out.
verses.after: “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me, crushed me, left me an empty vessel. He swallowed me like a monster, filled his belly with my delicacies, then cast me away.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me and crushed me; he made me an empty vessel. Like a sea monster he swallowed me; he filled his belly with my delicacies and cast me out.

verses.rationale: Keeps the personified woman's demand and flesh/blood parallelism.
verses.before: ‘May the violence done to me and my flesh be upon Babylon,’ the inhabitant of Zion will say. ‘And may my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,’ Jerusalem will say.”
verses.after: May the violence done to me and my flesh fall on Babylon,” says the woman dwelling in Zion. “May my blood fall on Chaldea's inhabitants,” says Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘May the violence done to me and my flesh be upon Babylon,’ the inhabitant of Zion will say. ‘And may my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,’ Jerusalem will say.”

verses.rationale: Preserves legal advocacy and water deprivation together.
verses.before: So thus says the LORD: “Look, I will plead your case and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and make her fountain dry.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the **LORD** says: “I will plead your case and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and make her spring run dry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore thus says the LORD: “Look, I will plead your case and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and make her fountain dry.

verses.rationale: Keeps all consequences and animal habitation.
verses.before: Babylon will become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.
verses.after: Babylon will become heaps of rubble, a haunt of jackals, a horror and an object of hissing, with no one living there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Babylon will become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Retains parallel animals and sounds without naming a new group.
verses.before: Together they roar like young lions; they growl like lion cubs.
verses.after: Together they roar like young lions, growl like lion cubs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Together they roar like young lions; they growl like lion cubs.

verses.rationale: Keeps the grotesque festive-to-death movement and ambiguous heat.
verses.before: When they are heated I will prepare their feast; I will make them drunk so that they become jubilant, then sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake,” says the LORD.
verses.after: When they are heated, I will prepare their feast and make them drunk, so they exult. Then they will sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they are heated I will prepare their feast; I will make them drunk so that they become jubilant, then sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three animal groups and sacrificial slaughter imagery.
verses.before: “I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter, like rams with male goats.
verses.after: “I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter, like rams with male goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter, like rams with male goats.

verses.rationale: Retains the cipher name and explicit Babylon parallel for the note to explain.
verses.before: “How Sheshach is captured! How the praise of the entire earth is seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
verses.after: How Sheshach is captured, the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
verses.tsw_comparator: “How Sheshach is captured! How the praise of the whole earth is seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!

verses.rationale: Keeps the flood image without identifying a literal sea.
verses.before: The sea has risen over Babylon; she is covered with the multitude of its waves.
verses.after: The sea has risen over Babylon; its roaring waves cover her.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sea has risen over Babylon; she is covered with the multitude of its waves.

verses.rationale: Preserves both absence of settlers and passersby.
verses.before: Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land and a wilderness, a land in which no one lives and through which no human being passes.
verses.after: Her towns have become a desolation, a dry and barren land, a land where no one lives and no human being passes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land and a wilderness, a land in which no one lives and through which no human being passes.

verses.rationale: Connects Bel's swallowing to the earlier monster image while retaining the streaming metaphor.
verses.before: I will attend to Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him, and even the wall of Babylon will fall.
verses.after: I will call Bel in Babylon to account and pull what he swallowed from his mouth. Nations will no longer stream to him. Even Babylon's wall has fallen.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will attend to Bel in Babylon and bring out of his mouth what he swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him, and even the wall of Babylon will fall.

verses.rationale: Retains the personal escape command and divine wrath.
verses.before: “Go out from the midst of her, my people! Each save his life from the burning anger of the LORD.
verses.after: Come out of her, my people! Save your lives, each of you, from the **LORD**'s burning anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Go out from the midst of her, my people! Each save his life from the burning anger of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Makes the recurring reports readable without manufacturing a timetable.
verses.before: Do not let your heart become weak, and do not fear because of the report heard in the land. A report comes in one year, and after it another report in another year: violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
verses.after: Do not lose heart or fear the reports heard in the land. One report comes one year, another the next: violence in the land, ruler against ruler.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not let your heart become weak, and do not fear because of the report heard in the land. A report comes in one year, and after it another report in another year: violence in the land, ruler against ruler.

verses.rationale: Keeps images, land, and slain as distinct objects of judgment.
verses.before: So look, days are coming when I will attend to the carved images of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
verses.after: Therefore days are coming when I will call Babylon's carved images to account. Her whole land will be disgraced; all her slain will fall within her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore look, days are coming when I will attend to the carved images of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.

verses.rationale: Preserves cosmic rejoicing over destruction without softening its force.
verses.before: Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will sing for joy over Babylon, for from the north the destroyers will come against her,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Heaven and earth and everything in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for destroyers will come against her from the north,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will sing for joy over Babylon, for from the north the destroyers will come against her,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses the retributive reading of the compressed clause and notes its difficulty.
verses.before: “As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon will fall the slain of all the land.
verses.after: Babylon must fall for Israel's slain, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: “As Babylon caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon will fall the slain of all the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement, distant remembrance, and the named city.
verses.before: “You who escaped the sword, go! Do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come upon your heart.
verses.after: You who escaped the sword, go on! Do not stand still. Remember the **LORD** from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You who escaped the sword, go! Do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come upon your heart.

verses.rationale: Marks the community's reply and retains plural holy places.
verses.before: ‘We are put to shame, for we have heard reproach; humiliation has covered our faces, for foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD’s house.’
verses.after: “We are ashamed, for we have heard insults; disgrace covers our faces. Foreigners have entered the holy places of the **LORD**'s house.”
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘We are put to shame, for we have heard reproach; humiliation has covered our faces, for foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD’s house.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the response to the community and wounded rather than painless disappearance.
verses.before: “Therefore look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will attend to her carved images, and throughout all her land the wounded will groan.
verses.after: “Therefore days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when I will call her carved images to account, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Therefore look, days are coming,” says the LORD, “when I will attend to her carved images, and throughout all her land the wounded will groan.

verses.rationale: Retains impossible ascent and direct divine sending.
verses.before: Though Babylon rises to the heavens, and though she fortifies the height of her strength, from me destroyers will come against her,” says the LORD.
verses.after: Though Babylon climbs to heaven and fortifies her lofty stronghold, destroyers will come to her from me,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though Babylon rises to the heavens, and though she fortifies the height of her strength, from me destroyers will come against her,” says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the brief announcement's two parallel halves.
verses.before: A sound of crying from Babylon, and great breaking from the land of the Chaldeans!
verses.after: A cry sounds from Babylon, great destruction from Chaldea's land!
verses.tsw_comparator: A sound of crying from Babylon, and great breaking from the land of the Chaldeans!

verses.rationale: Preserves the attackers' plural waves and voices without replacing the water image.
verses.before: For the LORD is devastating Babylon and silencing her great voice. Their waves roar like many waters; the roar of their voice is given.
verses.after: For the **LORD** is devastating Babylon, silencing her great voice. Their waves roar like mighty waters; the noise of their voices resounds.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD is devastating Babylon and silencing her great voice. Their waves roar like many waters; the roar of their voice is given.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated Babylon and emphatic repayment.
verses.before: For the destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. Her warriors are captured; their bows are shattered. For the LORD is a God of recompense; he will surely repay.
verses.after: A destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. Her warriors are captured; their bows are broken. For the **LORD** is a God of recompense; he will surely repay.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. Her warriors are captured; their bows are shattered. For the LORD is a God of recompense; he will surely repay.

verses.rationale: Retains the full administrative list and repeated death-sleep formula.
verses.before: “I will make her officials drunk, her wise men, her governors, her officers, and her warriors. They will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake,” says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: “I will make her officials and wise men drunk, her governors, deputies, and warriors. They will sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake,” declares the King, whose name is the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will make her officials drunk, her wise men, her governors, her officers, and her warriors. They will sleep an everlasting sleep and not wake,” says the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserves wasted labor and fire as the outcome of building.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The broad wall of Babylon will be utterly laid bare, and her high gates will be burned with fire. The peoples labor for emptiness, and the nations for fire, and they become weary.”
verses.after: This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Babylon's broad wall will be utterly stripped away, her high gates burned with fire. Peoples labor for nothing, nations wear themselves out for fire.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The broad wall of Babylon will be utterly laid bare, and her high gates will be burned with fire. The peoples labor for emptiness, and the nations for fire, and they become weary.”

verses.rationale: Keeps genealogy, companion journey, date, and uncertain office close to its literal wording.
verses.before: The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
verses.after: This is what Jeremiah the prophet instructed Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the officer responsible for resting places.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.

verses.rationale: Retains the single scroll and repeated totality.
verses.before: Jeremiah wrote in one book all the disaster that would come upon Babylon, all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
verses.after: Jeremiah wrote on a single scroll all the disaster that would come upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah wrote in one book all the disaster that would come upon Babylon, all these words that are written concerning Babylon.

verses.rationale: Renders see and read as deliberate attention to the reading task.
verses.before: Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words.
verses.after: Jeremiah told Seraiah, “When you reach Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words.

verses.rationale: Preserves the address, both creature groups, and duration.
verses.before: Then say, ‘O LORD, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off so that no one lives in it, from human to animal, but that it become an everlasting desolation.’
verses.after: Then say, ‘**LORD**, you have declared that this place will be cut off, with no one living in it, neither human nor animal. It will be a lasting desolation.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then say, ‘O LORD, you have spoken concerning this place, to cut it off so that no one lives in it, from human to animal, but that it become an everlasting desolation.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete symbolic action and named river.
verses.before: And when you have finished reading this book, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates.
verses.after: When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you have finished reading this book, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates.

verses.rationale: Retains the awkward final weariness clause and the book's internal closing formula rather than deleting either.
verses.before: Then say, ‘Thus Babylon will sink and will not rise because of the disaster that I am bringing upon her, and they will become weary.’” Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.
verses.after: Then say, ‘This is how Babylon will sink and never rise from the disaster I am bringing upon her. They will grow weary.’” Here end the words of Jeremiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then say, ‘Thus Babylon will sink and will not rise because of the disaster that I am bringing upon her, and they will become weary.’” Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

verses.rationale: Preserves ages, reign, maternal genealogy, and read name Hamutal.
verses.before: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.after: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the evaluation and comparison with the earlier king.
verses.before: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.after: He did what was evil in the **LORD**'s sight, just as Jehoiakim had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

verses.rationale: Makes the compressed causal statement readable and retains the separate rebellion notice.
verses.before: For because of the anger of the LORD this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them away from his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.after: Because of the **LORD**'s anger, events in Jerusalem and Judah reached the point where he cast them out of his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: For because of the anger of the LORD this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them away from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact date and surrounding siegeworks.
verses.before: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. They camped against it and built siegeworks against it all around.
verses.after: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped outside it and built siegeworks all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. They camped against it and built siegeworks against it all around.

verses.rationale: Keeps duration stated by regnal year rather than calculating it.
verses.before: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.after: The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

verses.rationale: Preserves exact day/month and lack of food.
verses.before: In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.after: By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was severe, and the people had no bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the escape route and surrounding force without harmonizing a singular king into this clause.
verses.before: Then the city was broken through, and all the men of war fled and went out from the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden, though the Chaldeans were around the city. They went toward the Arabah.
verses.after: Then the city wall was breached. All the fighting men fled from the city by night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden. With the Chaldeans surrounding the city, they took the road toward the Arabah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the city was broken through, and all the men of war fled and went out from the city by night by the way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden, though the Chaldeans were around the city. They went toward the Arabah.

verses.rationale: Preserves capture geography and abandonment.
verses.before: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
verses.after: The Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah on the plains of Jericho. His whole army had scattered away from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.

verses.rationale: Keeps Riblah's region and the judicial action.
verses.before: They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment upon him.
verses.after: They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he pronounced judgment on him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment upon him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the king's agency and repeated slaughter.
verses.before: The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. He also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
verses.after: The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah's sons before his eyes. He also slaughtered all Judah's officials at Riblah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. He also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.

verses.rationale: Keeps blinding, material, destination, and lifelong confinement.
verses.before: Then he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah, and the king of Babylon bound him with bronze chains, brought him to Babylon, and put him in prison until the day of his death.
verses.after: Then he blinded Zedekiah and bound him in bronze shackles. The king of Babylon took him to Babylon and kept him in custody until the day of his death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah, and the king of Babylon bound him with bronze chains, brought him to Babylon, and put him in prison until the day of his death.

verses.rationale: Preserves this date without harmonizing it to Kings.
verses.before: In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.after: On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated burning and distinct temple/palace/houses.
verses.before: He burned the house of the LORD, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.
verses.after: He burned the **LORD**'s house, the king's palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: He burned the house of the LORD, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comprehensive demolition.
verses.before: All the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.
verses.after: The whole Chaldean army with the captain of the guard tore down Jerusalem's walls all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Uses population for the difficult final collective, noting the possible artisans reading.
verses.before: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile some of the poor of the people, the rest of the people who remained in the city, people who had fallen away to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
verses.after: Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, carried into exile some of the poor, the people remaining in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the population.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile some of the poor of the people, the rest of the people who remained in the city, those who had fallen away to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.

verses.rationale: Keeps some poor deported and others left without erasing the distinction.
verses.before: Yet Nebuzaradan captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land as vineyard workers and farmers.
verses.after: But Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, left some of the poorest people of the land to tend vineyards and fields.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Nebuzaradan captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land as vineyard workers and farmers.

verses.rationale: Retains both divine names and the named Sea vessel.
verses.before: The Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the LORD, and carried all their bronze to Babylon.
verses.after: The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the **LORD**'s house, the stands, and the bronze Sea in the **LORD**'s house. They carried all their bronze to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the LORD, and carried all their bronze to Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full equipment list without merging items.
verses.before: They took the pots, shovels, snuffers, basins, spoons, and all the bronze vessels used in temple service.
verses.after: They took the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, basins, dishes, and all the bronze utensils used in service.
verses.tsw_comparator: They took the pots, shovels, snuffers, basins, spoons, and all the bronze vessels used in temple service.

verses.rationale: Keeps the second overlapping list and both precious metals.
verses.before: The captain of the guard took the bowls, firepans, basins, pots, lampstands, spoons, and bowls—what was gold as gold and what was silver as silver.
verses.after: The captain of the guard took the bowls, firepans, basins, pots, lampstands, dishes, and pouring bowls—everything made of gold or silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: The captain of the guard took the bowls, firepans, basins, pots, lampstands, spoons, and bowls—what was gold as gold and what was silver as silver.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult under-the-stands relation without harmonizing it; note addresses it.
verses.before: As for the two pillars, the one sea, the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD—the bronze of all these vessels could not be weighed.
verses.after: The two pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the **LORD**'s house—the bronze in all these objects was beyond weighing.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the two pillars, the one sea, the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD—the bronze of all these vessels could not be weighed.

verses.rationale: Keeps all dimensions and ancient units.
verses.before: As for the pillars, one pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits went around it. Its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow.
verses.after: Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits around, measured with a cord. It was hollow, with walls four fingers thick.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the pillars, one pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits went around it. Its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow.

verses.rationale: Preserves capital height, material, and matching second pillar.
verses.before: A bronze capital was upon it, and the height of one capital was five cubits. There was network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with pomegranates.
verses.after: On top was a bronze capital five cubits high, with latticework and pomegranates all around it, all of bronze. The second pillar had the same decoration and pomegranates.
verses.tsw_comparator: A bronze capital was upon it, and the height of one capital was five cubits. There was network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with pomegranates.

verses.rationale: Keeps both numbers without manufacturing a structural reconciliation.
verses.before: There were ninety-six pomegranates exposed to the wind; all the pomegranates on the network all around were one hundred.
verses.after: There were ninety-six pomegranates facing outward; a hundred pomegranates in all surrounded the latticework.
verses.tsw_comparator: There were ninety-six pomegranates exposed to the wind; all the pomegranates on the network all around were one hundred.

verses.rationale: Preserves all offices and the number of keepers.
verses.before: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.
verses.after: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three threshold keepers.
verses.tsw_comparator: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.

verses.rationale: Keeps one/seven/sixty and distinct offices; does not harmonize seven with Kings.
verses.before: From the city he took one court official who was appointed over the men of war, seven men from people who saw the king’s face who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found among the city.
verses.after: From the city he took one court official in charge of the fighting men, seven men who attended the king and were found in the city, the army commander's secretary who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the land found inside the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the city he took one court official who was appointed over the men of war, seven men from those who saw the king’s face who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.

verses.rationale: Retains both taking and transfer to the named place.
verses.before: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.after: Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.rationale: Preserves execution and the concluding removal from ground.
verses.before: The king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
verses.after: The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried into exile from its own ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the independent register's regnal year and exact number.
verses.before: These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, three thousand twenty-three Judeans;
verses.after: These are the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Judeans;
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, three thousand twenty-three Judeans;

verses.rationale: Preserves the second year and number without merging with the narrative date.
verses.before: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, eight hundred thirty-two persons from Jerusalem;
verses.after: in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year, 832 people from Jerusalem;
verses.tsw_comparator: in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, eight hundred thirty-two persons from Jerusalem;

verses.rationale: Retains the third deportation and the source total, which equals the listed counts.
verses.before: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile seven hundred forty-five Judeans. All the persons were four thousand six hundred.
verses.after: in Nebuchadnezzar's twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, carried away 745 Judeans. In all, 4,600 people.
verses.tsw_comparator: in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile seven hundred forty-five Judeans. All the persons were four thousand six hundred.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact date, king's name, and head-lifting image with its concrete outcome.
verses.before: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out from prison.
verses.after: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up Jehoiachin's head and released him from prison.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out from prison.

verses.rationale: Preserves the preferential seat and kindly speech without claiming restoration to Judah's throne.
verses.before: He spoke good things with him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.after: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the other kings with him in Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spoke good things with him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

verses.rationale: Makes the subject clear and renders eating before the king naturally.
verses.before: So Jehoiachin changed his prison garments and ate bread continually before the king all the days of his life.
verses.after: Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and ate regularly at the king's table for the rest of his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jehoiachin changed his prison garments and ate bread continually before the king all the days of his life.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated lifelong provision that closes the book.
verses.before: And for his allowance, a continual allowance was given to him by the king of Babylon, a daily portion, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
verses.after: The king of Babylon gave him a regular allowance, day by day, until his death, all the days of his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: And for his allowance, a continual allowance was given to him by the king of Babylon, a daily portion, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

comparative_references.scope: All 353 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
